definition_en: covered with something that clings, or difficult to deal with
core_image: 糖浆顺着手指慢慢往下滴
scene: 糖浆让她的手指发黏。 The syrup made her fingers sticky.
sceneCN: 这里 sticky 是「黏的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：糖浆让她的手指发黏。

derivatives.zh: 黏性
黏糊糊地

senses.title: Tending to cling
senses.definition: covered with a substance that sticks to whatever it touches
senses.definitionCN: 覆有碰到什么就粘住什么的物质
senses.example: The syrup made her fingers sticky.
senses.exampleCN: 糖浆让她的手指发黏。
senses.why: This is the physical sense you feel.
senses.whyCN: 这是能摸到的物理义项。

senses.title: Hot and damp
senses.definition: unpleasantly warm and humid, so that the skin feels damp
senses.definitionCN: 闷热潮湿，皮肤黏腻不适
senses.example: It was a sticky summer evening.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个闷热的夏夜。
senses.why: Damp skin feels sticky in heat.
senses.whyCN: 天热时潮湿的皮肤会有黏腻感。

senses.title: Hard to handle
senses.definition: difficult and awkward to deal with
senses.definitionCN: 难以应付、让人为难的
senses.example: We are in a sticky situation.
senses.exampleCN: 我们处在棘手的局面中。
senses.why: A sticky surface traps the hand, and a sticky problem traps the mind.
senses.whyCN: 黏的表面困住手，棘手的问题困住头脑。

intro.en: Sticky is stick plus -y, formed in Middle English from the verb stick.
intro.cn: sticky 是 stick 加 -y，在中古英语中由动词 stick 构成。

items.en: Sticca named a twig.
items.cn: sticca 指细枝。

items.en: Sticken meant to pierce or fasten.
items.cn: sticken 意为刺入或固定。

items.en: Sticky described a clinging surface.
items.cn: sticky 描述黏附的表面。

items.en: Sticky spread to humid weather.
items.cn: sticky 扩展到潮湿的天气。

items.en: It also named a difficult problem.
items.cn: 它也开始指难办的问题。

note.en: Sticky is compared with look-alike words and with words for clinging and difficulty.
note.cn: 把 sticky 与形近词以及表示黏附和困难的词作比较。

entries.definition: a thin piece of wood
entries.definitionCN: 棍

entries.definition: short and strong
entries.definitionCN: 矮壮的

entries.definition: fashionable and attractive
entries.definitionCN: 时髦的

entries.definition: able to stick to a surface
entries.definitionCN: 有黏性的

entries.definition: warm and wet
entries.definitionCN: 潮湿的

entries.definition: difficult to handle
entries.definitionCN: 棘手的

normalIntro.en: Sticky is a hand you cannot wipe dry, air you cannot shake off, and a problem you cannot put down.
normalIntro.cn: sticky 是擦不干的手，是甩不掉的空气，也是放不下的难题。

normal.en: Honey leaves sticky fingers.
normal.cn: 蜂蜜会让手指发黏。

normal.en: Use sticky tape to seal the box.
normal.cn: 用胶带封住盒子。

normal.en: The weather is hot and sticky.
normal.cn: 天气又热又黏。

normal.en: They are in a sticky situation.
normal.cn: 他们处境棘手。

normal.en: Sticky rice holds together.
normal.cn: 糯米能粘在一起。

abstract.en: Some memories are sticky and will not wipe off.
abstract.cn: 有些记忆很黏，擦不掉。

abstract.en: A sticky problem holds the mind the way glue holds paper.
abstract.cn: 棘手的问题抓住头脑，就像胶抓住纸。

abstract.en: What feels sticky now may be what keeps things together.
abstract.cn: 此刻黏手的东西，也许正是把一切连住的东西。

examples.en: The syrup made her fingers sticky.
examples.cn: 糖浆让她的手指发黏。

examples.en: We are in a sticky situation.
examples.cn: 我们处在棘手的局面中。

examples.en: It was a sticky summer evening.
examples.cn: 那是个闷热的夏夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: sticky 是 stick 加 -y，「黏的」；sticky tape 是胶带，sticky rice 是糯米；天气闷热潮湿也叫 sticky，棘手的局面是 a sticky situation。

root: stick（粘）加形容词后缀 -y；由物理上的黏附，引申为皮肤黏腻的闷热天气与难以脱身的棘手局面。

sensesIntro.en: Sticky means clinging to the touch, damp with heat, or awkward to deal with.
sensesIntro.cn: sticky 指触之黏手、因热而潮湿，或难以应付。

core.en: A surface that holds the finger.
core.cn: 留住手指的表面。

branches.en: Syrup runs down a fingertip.
branches.cn: 糖浆顺着指尖流下。

branches.en: A shirt holds to the back in summer.
branches.cn: 夏天衬衫贴在背上。

branches.en: A question has no easy answer.
branches.cn: 一个问题没有轻松的答案。

branches.en: Heat and sugar both make the skin cling.
branches.cn: 热与糖，都会让皮肤发黏。

branches.en: A sticky thing and a sticky problem both refuse to let go.
branches.cn: 黏手的东西与棘手的问题，都不肯放人。

intro.en: Sticky takes comparison and builds a noun and an adverb.
intro.cn: sticky 加比较级，并构成名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

definition_zh: 一条面包；块状食物；游荡；闲混；（俚）脑袋
definition_en: a whole bread baked in one piece, a food shaped into a solid block, to spend time idly, or in British slang the head
core_image: 刚出炉的长条面包摆在木桌上，表皮金黄，被人用手按出一处浅浅的凹痕
scene: 清晨的面包房里，师傅把刚出炉的长条面包一列排开，热气在玻璃上凝成水雾。 She cut a thick slice from the loaf and spread it with butter.
sceneCN: 这里 loaf 是「一条面包」（第 1 个义项：整条烤出的面包）；句意为她从整条面包上切下厚厚一片，抹上黄油。图中可辨识物件：木桌、金黄面包、玻璃上的水雾。

pos.zh: 一条面包；块状食物；（俚）脑袋

derivatives.zh: 由 loaf 加 -er 构成，义为「游手好闲的人」，后又指一种平底船鞋
由 loaf 加 -ing 构成，义为「闲荡；磨洋工」
由 meat 与 loaf 复合，义为「肉糕」，指烤成块状的碎肉

senses.title: A whole bread baked in one piece
senses.definition: a bread baked as one rounded or oblong piece, before it is cut into slices
senses.definitionCN: 烤成一整块、尚未切片的面包，形状多为圆形或长条形
senses.example: She cut a thick slice from the loaf and spread it with butter.
senses.exampleCN: 她从整条面包上切下厚厚一片，抹上黄油。
senses.why: Old English hlaf named bread as a baked whole, and the unit rather than the substance is what the word has always counted.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hlaf 把面包指认为一整块烤成的东西，这个词从古至今计量的是「一个整体」，而不是面包这种材料。

senses.title: Food pressed into a solid block
senses.definition: food, especially meat or sugar, shaped and cooked into a solid block
senses.definitionCN: 把食物，尤指肉或糖，压成并煮成坚实的块状
senses.example: The meat loaf came out of the oven with a crust of browned fat.
senses.exampleCN: 肉糕出炉时表面结着一层焦黄的油脂。
senses.why: A baked loaf is a mass held together by heat, and cooks reuse that picture whenever they press minced meat or boiled sugar into one solid shape.
senses.whyCN: 烤好的面包是靠热力聚成的一块，厨子把碎肉或熬好的糖压成整块时，便重复了这幅图景。

senses.title: To spend time doing nothing
senses.definition: to pass time without working or without a clear purpose, often while moving about
senses.definitionCN: 不干活、也没有明确目的地消磨时间，常常是四处走动
senses.example: He loafed about the harbour all afternoon, watching the boats come in.
senses.exampleCN: 他整个下午都在港口闲逛，看船进港。
senses.why: The verb appeared centuries after the bread word and its origin is uncertain; it paints idleness as time left to lie around like dough waiting to be shaped.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词比面包那个词晚了好几百年才出现，来源不确定；它把闲散画成一段像面团一样摊着、等着被塑形的时间。

senses.title: The head, in British slang
senses.definition: the head, used in informal British speech and in the phrase use your loaf
senses.definitionCN: 脑袋，用于英式非正式口语，常见于 use your loaf 这一说法
senses.example: Use your loaf and check the timetable before you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 动动脑子，出门前先看看时刻表。
senses.why: Rhyming slang replaced the word for head with a phrase, loaf of bread, and then shortened the phrase to loaf; the bread word thereby acquired a second bodily sense.
senses.whyCN: 押韵俚语用 loaf of bread 这个短语代替「头」这个词，随后又把它缩成 loaf；面包这个词因此多出一个身体义项。

intro.en: Loaf is an Old English word for a baked bread; the verb meaning to idle is much later and its origin is genuinely uncertain.
intro.cn: loaf 是古英语中表示「烤好的面包」的词；表示闲荡的动词出现得晚得多，来源确实不确定。

items.en: Hlaf meant bread as a baked whole, and it also entered compounds for the giver of bread, the hlaford, later lord.
items.cn: hlaf 指一整块烤好的面包，它还进入复合词，用来指分面包的人 hlaford，也就是后来的 lord。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form is hlaibaz, and German Laib and Gothic hlaifs are its close relatives.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式是 hlaibaz，德语 Laib 与哥特语 hlaifs 都是它的近亲。

items.en: Middle English lof keeps the baked sense, and its plural loaves settles the f that turns into v between vowels.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lof 保留「烤好的面包」义，复数 loaves 固定了 f 在两个元音之间变成 v 的规律。

items.en: The verb loaf, meaning to idle, is first recorded in the nineteenth century; dictionaries call its origin uncertain and only suggest a loose link with loiter.
items.cn: 表示闲荡的动词 loaf 最早见于十九世纪；词典称其来源不确定，只提出与 loiter 有松散的关联。

items.en: Modern English adds meat loaf and sugar loaf, and rhyming slang turns loaf of bread into a slang word for the head.
items.cn: 现代英语加上肉糕与糖锥，押韵俚语又把 loaf of bread 变成指脑袋的俚语词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the plural form, one derivative, a German relative and a word that merely looks similar; the near-meaning group collects other bread shapes.
note.cn: 形近组收复数形式、一个派生词、一个德语同族词，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；近义组收其他面包形态的词。

entries.definition: The plural of loaf, with f changed to v before the ending.
entries.definitionCN: loaf 的复数形式，词尾前 f 变为 v。

entries.definition: An idle person, and also a slip-on shoe.
entries.definitionCN: 游手好闲的人；也指一种平底便鞋；由 loaf 加 -er 构成。

entries.definition: The German word for a loaf or a round mass of bread.
entries.definitionCN: 德语中表示一条或一块圆形面包的词，与 loaf 同源。

entries.definition: An upper floor or a raised space under a roof; only the spelling is close, the origin is different.
entries.definitionCN: 阁楼；屋顶下的高起空间；与 loaf 只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The baked food made from flour, usually named as a substance rather than counted.
entries.definitionCN: 面粉烤成的食物，通常作为不可数的材料来指称，而 loaf 计量的是整条。

entries.definition: A small round bread, often sweet.
entries.definitionCN: 小圆面包，常带甜味。

entries.definition: A small loaf or bread shaped by rolling the dough.
entries.definitionCN: 小面包；把面团卷成形的面包。

entries.definition: A long narrow French loaf with a crisp crust.
entries.definitionCN: 法式长棍面包；细长、外壳酥脆。

normalIntro.en: The word starts as bread counted by the piece, and its family keeps returning to baked masses, idle time and one slang head.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是把面包按「个」来数，它的同族词反复回到烤成的块、闲散的时间，以及一个俚语里的脑袋。

normal.en: Old English hlaf meant a baked bread, and the same root gave hlaford, the bread giver who became the lord.
normal.cn: 古英语 hlaf 指烤好的面包，同一个词根还给出 hlaford，即分面包的人，后来成为 lord。

normal.en: German Laib and Gothic hlaifs are close cousins, so the bread sense is shared across the Germanic family.
normal.cn: 德语 Laib 与哥特语 hlaifs 是近亲，面包义项在整个日耳曼语族中相通。

normal.en: The plural loaves shows the old rule that f becomes v between two vowels, as in leaf and leaves.
normal.cn: 复数 loaves 体现了 f 在两个元音之间变 v 的古老规则，就像 leaf 与 leaves 一样。

normal.en: Meat loaf and sugar loaf borrow the shape of a baked block, not the bread itself.
normal.cn: meat loaf 与 sugar loaf 借的是烤成的一块这个形状，而不是面包本身。

normal.en: To use your loaf is rhyming slang: loaf of bread stood for head, and the phrase was cut down to one word.
normal.cn: use your loaf 属于押韵俚语：loaf of bread 代替 head，后来整个短语被缩成一个词。

abstract.en: A loaf is bread treated as a single object, which is why the word counts pieces while bread names a material.
abstract.cn: loaf 是把面包当成一个整体物件，所以它数「条」，而 bread 指的是材料。

abstract.en: The same word for a solid baked block later describes a person standing about doing nothing, as if time itself were dough.
abstract.cn: 同一个表示烤成实心块的词，后来用来形容人站着什么都不做，仿佛时间本身也是面团。

abstract.en: English took the sound of a bread phrase and made it a word for the mind, showing how slang can carry a body part on a bakery image.
abstract.cn: 英语借一个面包短语的声音造出指头脑的词，说明俚语能让身体部位搭在烘焙的意象上。

examples.en: She cut a thick slice from the loaf and spread it with butter.
examples.cn: 她从整条面包上切下厚厚一片，抹上黄油。

examples.en: He loafed about the harbour all afternoon, watching the boats come in.
examples.cn: 他整个下午都在港口闲逛，看船进港。

examples.en: Use your loaf and check the timetable before you leave.
examples.cn: 动动脑子，出门前先看看时刻表。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「老富」——老富有钱却不肯干活，整天在街上晃；loaf 是游荡，也是一条面包。

root: 古英语 hlaf（烤好的面包），与德语 Laib、哥特语 hlaifs 同源；表示「闲荡」的动词晚出，来源不确定，一般认为可能与 loiter 有松散关联。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one baked bread; the senses then divide into food pressed into a block, the later verb for idling, and a rhyming-slang head.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一整条烤好的面包；义项由此分成压成块的食物、晚出的闲荡动词，以及押韵俚语里的脑袋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a golden loaf on a wooden board, one thumb print pressed into its warm crust.
core.cn: 核心意象：木板上一条金黄的面包，温热的外皮上按着一个拇指印。

branches.en: a baker sliding fresh loaves onto a cooling rack
branches.cn: 面包师把新出炉的面包放上晾架

branches.en: a meat loaf steaming beside a knife
branches.cn: 肉糕冒着热气，旁边放着刀

branches.en: a cone of hard sugar standing on a counter
branches.cn: 柜台上立着一个硬糖锥

branches.en: a man drifting past closed shop fronts
branches.cn: 一个人晃过一间间关门的店铺

branches.en: a friend tapping his temple in a joke
branches.cn: 朋友开玩笑地敲了敲太阳穴

intro.en: The word is a Germanic noun for baked bread, and English stacks a plural, an agent suffix and compounds on that base.
intro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中表示烤面包的名词，英语在这个词基上加上复数、施事后缀与复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; Latin panis means bread, but it is a different root with no shared ancestry.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；拉丁语 panis 意为「面包」，但那是另一个词根，并无共同来源。

items.meaning: a whole bread, a shaped block
minced meat baked as a block

definition_en: following the popular style of the time, visited by stylish people, or widely accepted
core_image: 穿着剪裁利落风衣的人走进咖啡馆，众人纷纷抬头
scene: 那位时髦的女士走进了咖啡馆。 The fashionable woman walked into the cafe.
sceneCN: 这里 fashionable 是「时髦的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：那位时髦的女士走进了咖啡馆。

pos.zh: 上流社会的；时髦人士常去的

derivatives.zh: 时尚
时髦地
过时的
时尚达人

senses.title: Following current style
senses.definition: popular and considered stylish at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 在某一时期流行并被认为有品位的
senses.example: She wore a fashionable coat to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一件时髦的外套去参加聚会。
senses.why: The central sense is matching the current style.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是符合当下的风格。

senses.title: Frequented by stylish people
senses.titleCN: 上流社会的；时髦人士常去的
senses.definition: used or visited by people of high social position
senses.definitionCN: 社会地位高的人使用或光顾的
senses.example: They dined at a fashionable restaurant.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一家上流人士常去的餐厅用餐。
senses.why: Places borrow the label from the people who gather there.
senses.whyCN: 场所因聚集于此的人而获得这一标签。

senses.title: Widely accepted
senses.definition: common or accepted among many people at a time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期在许多人中普遍或被接受的
senses.example: That opinion is fashionable among economists.
senses.exampleCN: 那种观点在经济学家中很流行。
senses.why: The sense widens from clothes to accepted ideas.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项从服装扩大到被接受的观点。

intro.en: Fashionable is fashion plus able, meaning fit for or following the current style.
intro.cn: fashionable 是 fashion 加 able，意为符合或追随当下风格的。

items.en: Façon, a manner or style, entered English as fashion.
items.cn: façon（方式、样式）进入英语后成为 fashion。

items.en: The suffix able formed words meaning fit for something.
items.cn: 后缀 able 构成表示「适合某事」的词。

items.en: Fashionable meant conforming to current style.
items.cn: fashionable 意为符合当下风格。

items.en: It also described places visited by high society.
items.cn: 它也用于描述上流社会光顾的场所。

items.en: Fashionable now means stylish or widely popular.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fashionable 意为时髦或广泛流行。

note.en: Fashionable is compared with related forms and with adjectives for style.
note.cn: 把 fashionable 与相关词形以及表示风格品位的形容词作比较。

entries.definition: in a stylish way
entries.definitionCN: 时髦地

entries.definition: no longer stylish
entries.definitionCN: 过时的

entries.definition: able to be understood
entries.definitionCN: 可理解的

entries.definition: attractive and well designed
entries.definitionCN: 有品位的；时髦的

entries.definition: following the latest trend
entries.definitionCN: 紧跟潮流的

entries.definition: elegantly stylish
entries.definitionCN: 别致的；优雅时髦的

normalIntro.en: Fashion plus able gives fashionable, able to follow fashion.
normalIntro.cn: fashion 加 able 就是 fashionable，即能跟上时尚的。

normal.en: Fashionable clothes look new and stylish.
normal.cn: fashionable 的衣服看起来新颖时髦。

normal.en: Unfashionable is the opposite.
normal.cn: unfashionable 是它的反义词。

normal.en: A fashionable district is full of stylish shops.
normal.cn: 时尚街区满是时髦店铺。

normal.en: Fashionably late is a joking phrase.
normal.cn: fashionably late 是一个玩笑说法。

normal.en: Fashionable is stronger on taste than popular.
normal.cn: fashionable 比 popular 更强调品味。

abstract.en: The suffix able marks the ability to meet a standard.
abstract.cn: 后缀 able 表示符合某种标准的能力。

abstract.en: Fashion is a group standard, so fashionable is always social.
abstract.cn: 时尚是群体标准，因此 fashionable 总带有社会性。

abstract.en: A place becomes fashionable because the right people gather there.
abstract.cn: 一个地方因合适的人聚集而变得时髦。

examples.en: She wore a fashionable coat to the party.
examples.cn: 她穿了一件时髦的外套去参加聚会。

examples.en: The restaurant is popular with fashionable crowds.
examples.cn: 这家餐厅很受时髦人群欢迎。

examples.en: Long skirts became fashionable again.
examples.cn: 长裙又流行起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: fashion 是「时尚」，able 表示「能……的」，fashionable 就是「能跟上时尚的、时髦的」。

root: 由 fashion（时尚）加形容词后缀 able 构成，fashion 源自拉丁语 facere（做）。

sensesIntro.en: Fashionable means following current style, frequented by stylish people, or widely accepted.
sensesIntro.cn: fashionable 意为符合当下风格、时髦人士常去的，或被广泛接受的。

core.en: Matching the taste and style a group approves.
core.cn: 符合当下品味与群体审美的。

branches.en: Dressed in the current style.
branches.cn: 穿着当下风格。

core_image: 两个氧原子被一条看不见的弹簧拉住，独自成团地飘在空气里

senses.title: The chemical unit: atoms bonded into one group
senses.titleCN: 化学分子：原子成键组成的整体
senses.definition: the smallest unit of a substance that keeps its chemical identity, made of atoms held together by chemical bonds
senses.definitionCN: 保持物质化学性质的最小单元，由化学键连接的原子组成
senses.example: A water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
senses.exampleCN: 一个水分子含两个氢原子和一个氧原子。
senses.why: Molecule began as Latin molecula, 'a little mass'. Chemistry narrowed it to the smallest group of bonded atoms that still behaves as the substance, so the word moved from 'small lump' to 'bonded unit'.
senses.whyCN: molecule 最初是拉丁语 molecula「一小团物质」。化学把它收窄为仍然表现为该物质的最小成键原子团，于是词义从「小团块」转成「成键单元」。

senses.title: A tiny particle of matter
senses.definition: a very small particle of a substance, considered without regard to its internal bonds
senses.definitionCN: 物质中极小的颗粒，不考虑其内部成键情况
senses.example: Dust molecules coated the mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 灰尘微粒覆盖了镜面。
senses.why: The older, looser sense survives in ordinary speech, where any very small piece of matter may be called a molecule. Here the word means size, not chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 较旧、较松的义项在日常语言中留存，任何极小的物质碎屑都可能被称为 molecule。此处词义指的是大小，而不是化学。

senses.title: Biological macromolecule: proteins, DNA, starch
senses.titleCN: 生物大分子：蛋白质、DNA、淀粉
senses.definition: a very large molecule built from many repeating units, especially one found in living things
senses.definitionCN: 由许多重复单元构成的极大分子，尤指存在于生物体中的
senses.example: Each cell contains thousands of protein molecules.
senses.exampleCN: 每个细胞含有数千个蛋白质分子。
senses.why: Biology called its long chains molecules because they are bonded units, then added macro- when the size became the point. The base word keeps its chemical sense throughout.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把长链称为 molecule，因为它们就是成键单元；当大小成为重点时，又加上 macro-。词基本身始终保留化学义。

senses.title: Single-molecule work: studying one at a time
senses.titleCN: 单分子：一次只研究一个
senses.definition: in research, one individual molecule examined or manipulated on its own rather than in bulk
senses.definitionCN: 研究中指被单独观测或操作的那一个分子，而不是整批
senses.example: Single-molecule imaging revealed the folding steps.
senses.exampleCN: 单分子成像揭示了折叠的各个步骤。
senses.why: When instruments became sharp enough, the word needed a countable singular. Single-molecule marks the shift from averaging a crowd to watching one individual.
senses.whyCN: 当仪器足够精细时，这个词需要一个可数的单数形式。single-molecule 标记了从对一群分子取平均，转为观察单个分子的转变。

senses.title: The independent unit in a gas or liquid
senses.titleCN: 气体或液体中的独立单元
senses.definition: the separate unit that moves independently in a gas or solution, as opposed to a continuous network
senses.definitionCN: 在气体或溶液中独立运动的单元，与连续网络相对
senses.example: Gas molecules collide millions of times each second.
senses.exampleCN: 气体分子每秒碰撞数百万次。
senses.why: Kinetic theory needs a unit that travels freely. A molecule is exactly that: a bonded group small enough to move as one body through a fluid.
senses.whyCN: 动理论需要一个能自由行进的单元。分子正合适：那是一个小到能作为一个整体在流体中运动的成键原子团。

senses.title: A trace: a molecule of something
senses.definition: an extremely small amount of something, used in phrases such as not a molecule of truth
senses.definitionCN: 极少的量，用在 not a molecule of truth（一点真相也没有）一类的说法中
senses.example: There is not a molecule of evidence for that claim.
senses.exampleCN: 那个主张连一丝证据都没有。
senses.why: Because a molecule is invisibly small, the word can mean 'the least possible amount'. The metaphor borrows the chemist's smallest unit for the smallest imaginable trace.
senses.whyCN: 因为分子小到不可见，这个词可以表示「可能的最少量」。这一比喻借化学家的最小单位，指想象所及的最微小痕迹。

senses.title: The repeating unit of a polymer
senses.definition: in polymer chemistry, the repeating structural unit from which a long chain is built
senses.definitionCN: 高分子化学中指构成长链的重复结构单元
senses.example: Each molecule in the chain repeats the same pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 链中的每个单元重复着同一模式。
senses.why: Here the word names the brick rather than the wall. Polymer science counts how many molecule units are joined, so molecule marks the unit of repetition.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指的是砖，而不是墙。高分子科学要数有多少个分子单元被连起来，因此 molecule 标记的是重复单位。

senses.title: A minute element of a larger thing
senses.titleCN: 微小成分：大事物里的一小点
senses.definition: a very small element or ingredient within a larger whole, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 较大整体中极小的成分或要素，用于比喻
senses.example: A molecule of doubt remained in his mind.
senses.exampleCN: 他心里还留着一丝疑虑。
senses.why: The figurative sense treats an idea as a substance with parts. One molecule of doubt is the smallest part that still counts as doubt, exactly as a molecule is the smallest part that still counts as the substance.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义把念头当作有组成部分的物质。一丝疑虑就是还算得上疑虑的最小部分，正如一个分子是还算得上该物质的最小部分。

intro.en: Molecule comes through French molécule from Latin molecula, a diminutive of moles 'mass, heap, massive structure'. The early sense was simply 'a small mass'. Modern chemistry fixed the meaning as a bonded group of atoms in the early 19th century, after Avogadro distinguished molecules from atoms. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: molecule 经法语 molécule 来自拉丁语 molecula，即 moles「块体、堆、庞大结构」的指小形式。早期义只是「一小团物质」。现代化学在 19 世纪初把词义固定为成键的原子团，此前阿伏伽德罗已区分分子与原子。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Chemistry fixes molecule as a bonded group of atoms, and single-molecule work appears much later with sharper instruments.
items.cn: 化学把 molecule 固定为成键的原子团；单分子研究则要晚得多，随着更精细的仪器才出现。

items.en: English molecule is borrowed in the general sense of a small mass or particle, before any chemical definition.
items.cn: 英语 molecule 在尚无化学定义时借入，泛指一小团物质或微粒。

items.en: French molécule is coined from the Latin diminutive as part of early corpuscular theory.
items.cn: 法语 molécule 由拉丁指小形式造出，属于早期微粒说的一部分。

items.en: molecula is moles 'mass' plus the diminutive -cula; it means a small mass, not a bonded group.
items.cn: molecula 是 moles「块体」加指小成分 -cula，意为小团物质，不是成键的原子团。

items.en: The origin of moles beyond Latin is of uncertain origin and is not securely tied to a reconstructed root.
items.cn: moles 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，未能可靠地系于某个重构词根。

note.en: The first group separates three words that look related but are not, or are related only in one sense; the second compares units of matter at different levels.
note.cn: 第一组把三个看似相关、实则无关或只在某一义上相关的词分开；第二组比较不同层级上的物质单元。

entries.definition: a small burrowing animal. This word comes from Germanic roots and has no connection with molecula, despite the identical spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 一种小型穴居动物。这个词出自日耳曼词根，尽管拼写相同，却与 molecula 无关。

entries.definition: a small heap of earth thrown up by a burrowing mole. It belongs with the animal sense, not with the chemical unit.
entries.definitionCN: 鼹鼠刨出的小土堆，属于动物义那一支，与化学单位义无关。

entries.definition: a grinding tooth, from Latin mola 'millstone'. The chemistry adjective molar comes from mole instead, so the two meanings have different histories.
entries.definitionCN: 磨牙，出自拉丁语 mola「磨石」。化学形容词 molar 则出自 mole，两个含义历史不同。

entries.definition: the smallest unit of an element. Atoms are the parts that molecules are built from, so the two words mark different levels.
entries.definitionCN: 元素的最小单元。原子是构成分子的部件，因此两词标记不同层级。

entries.definition: a very small piece of matter. It says nothing about bonds, and may even be larger than a molecule.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的物质碎块。它不涉及成键，甚至可能比分子还大。

entries.definition: a substance made of two or more elements chemically joined. It names a material, while molecule names one unit of it.
entries.definitionCN: 由两种或以上元素化学结合而成的物质。它命名一种材料，而 molecule 命名该材料的一个单元。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The -cule is a diminutive, so molecule literally begins as 'a small mass'.
normal.cn: -cule 是指小成分，所以 molecule 字面上起于「一小团物质」。

normal.en: Moles also gives demolish, 'to take the mass down', and mole as a breakwater, 'a mass built out'.
normal.cn: moles 还给出 demolish「把块体拆下」以及作防波堤解的 mole「向外筑起的块体」。

normal.en: The chemical unit and the unit of amount are linked: mole is simply molecule shortened.
normal.cn: 化学分子与物质的量单位是相连的：mole 就是 molecule 的缩略。

normal.en: The animal mole shares spelling but not history, so it never appears in chemistry.
normal.cn: 动物义的 mole 只是拼写相同，历史不同，因此从不进入化学语境。

normal.en: A molecule is the smallest piece that still behaves like the substance: split it and the substance is gone.
normal.cn: 分子是仍然表现得像该物质的最小部分：再切开，该物质就不存在了。

abstract.en: See two balls joined by a spring drifting as one body through empty space.
abstract.cn: 想象两个小球被一根弹簧连着，作为一个整体在空处漂移。

abstract.en: Every sense treats the molecule as a smallest whole: smallest unit, smallest particle, smallest trace, smallest ingredient.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都把分子当作一个最小的整体：最小单元、最小颗粒、最少痕迹、最小成分。

abstract.en: The word sits one floor above the atom and one floor below the material.
abstract.cn: 这个词位于原子之上、材料之下的一层。

examples.en: Ozone is a molecule of three oxygen atoms.
examples.cn: 臭氧是由三个氧原子构成的分子。

examples.en: The enzyme breaks each starch molecule into sugars.
examples.cn: 这种酶把每个淀粉分子分解成糖。

examples.en: Not a molecule of the original text survives.
examples.cn: 原文一丝一毫都没有留存下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莫利Q」——莫利把Q弹的两个小球连成一小团，飘着走 → molecule 分子

root: 拉丁语 moles「块体、堆」＋指小成分 -cula → molecula「一小团物质」→ 法语 molécule → 英语 molecule。核心是「小到仍是该物质的最小一团」，化学把它定为成键的原子团。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: the smallest group that still counts as the thing. What changes is the frame — a chemical unit, a dust particle, a long biological chain, one observed individual, a free-flying gas unit, a trace, a repeating brick in a polymer, or a small ingredient of an idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：仍然算得上「该物」的最小一团。变化的只是框架——化学单元、尘埃颗粒、生物长链、被观测的单个个体、自由飞行的气体单元、一丝痕迹、聚合物中的重复砖块，还是一个念头里的小成分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two oxygen atoms held by an invisible bond, drifting as one group.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个氧原子被看不见的键拉着，作为一个整体漂移。

branches.en: THE CHEMICAL UNIT: Latin 'small mass' becomes a bonded group, and long biological chains are still such groups.
branches.cn: 化学单元：拉丁语「小团」变成成键原子团，生物长链也仍是这样的原子团。

branches.en: MERE SIZE: in everyday use any very small particle may be called a molecule, with no chemistry implied.
branches.cn: 仅指大小：日常用法中任何极小的颗粒都可叫 molecule，不含化学意味。

branches.en: ONE UNIT VERSUS MANY: single-molecule work watches one, while kinetic theory treats each as a free traveller.
branches.cn: 一个与许多：单分子研究观察一个，动理论则把每个都当作自由行者。

branches.en: THE TRACE: the smallest imaginable amount borrows the chemist's smallest unit.
branches.cn: 痕迹：想象所及的最少量，借用了化学家的最小单位。

branches.en: THE BRICK AND THE INGREDIENT: polymers repeat one unit, and ideas are said to contain molecules of doubt.
branches.cn: 砖块与成分：聚合物重复同一单元，念头里则被说成含有「一丝」疑虑。

intro.en: Molecule is Latin molecula, a diminutive in -cula built on moles 'mass'. Its English relatives attach the suffixes -ar, -ity and the prefixes macro- and bi-.
intro.cn: molecule 是拉丁语 molecula，由 moles「块体」加指小成分 -cula 构成。它的英语同族词接上 -ar、-ity 后缀以及 macro-、bi- 前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are moles 'mass, heap' and the diminutive -cula. moles also gives demolish and mole in the sense of a breakwater.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁成分是 moles「块体、堆」与指小成分 -cula。moles 还给出 demolish 以及作防波堤解的 mole。

items.example: Each molecule of water is bent, not straight.
items.exampleCN: 每个水分子都是弯的，不是直的。

items.example: The two forms are molecularly identical.
items.exampleCN: 这两种形式在分子层面完全相同。

items.exampleCN: 两摩尔气体充满这个烧瓶。

normal.en: Do not speak rudely to the staff.

normal.en: We were rudely woken by hammering.

normal.en: The question was rudely worded.

senses.title: Almost not
senses.definition: only just, in a way that is almost not true
senses.definitionCN: 只差一点就不能，程度极低
senses.example: I could barely see the road ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 我几乎看不清前面的路。
senses.why: Barely is bare plus -ly, and bare means 'nothing extra', so barely marks a point with nothing to spare.
senses.whyCN: barely 是 bare 加 -ly，而 bare 意为「没有多余」，所以 barely 标记的是毫无余量的那一点。

senses.title: Only just
senses.definition: by only a small amount or margin
senses.definitionCN: 只差很小的量或幅度
senses.example: We had barely enough money for the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的钱勉强够坐公交。
senses.why: When a supply has no surplus, just enough is barely enough, which gives the sense of a narrow margin.
senses.whyCN: 当供给没有剩余时，刚好够就等于勉强够，于是产生「只差一点」的含义。

definition_en: a female domestic servant; also a young unmarried woman in literary use, or a woman who attends a bride at a wedding
core_image: 白色围裙系在腰间，手里端着一叠刚熨好的床单
scene: 清晨的旧宅里，楼梯扶手还带着前一夜的灰尘，厨房的水壶已经烧开。 By the time the family woke, the maid had polished every brass handle in the hall.
sceneCN: 这里指受雇料理家务的女性（第 1 个义项：女仆）；句意为家人醒来时，女仆已把门厅里每个铜把手擦亮。

derivatives.zh: 由中古英语 maide 加指小后缀 -en 演变而来，义为「少女；未婚女子」
由 maiden 加 -ly 构成，义为「少女般的；端庄的」
由 bar 与 maid 复合，义为「酒吧女侍者」

senses.title: A female domestic servant
senses.definition: a woman employed to clean, cook and do household work for a family
senses.definitionCN: 受雇为家庭打扫、做饭、料理家务的女性
senses.example: The maid changed the sheets every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 女仆每天早上更换床单。
senses.why: Old English mægden first meant a young unmarried woman, and in large households those young women were the ones given indoor work, so the word came to name the job itself.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mægden 本指年轻的未婚女子，而大户人家里正是这些年轻女子被安排做室内杂活，于是这个词转而指这份工作。

senses.title: A young unmarried woman
senses.definition: a girl or young woman who is not married, a use now mostly found in literature
senses.definitionCN: 未结婚的少女或年轻女子，这一用法如今多见于文学作品
senses.example: In the old ballad, a maid waits by the river for her sailor.
senses.exampleCN: 在那首古老歌谣里，一位少女在河边等候她的水手。
senses.why: Before girl and woman became the everyday words, maid was the ordinary term for a young unmarried female, and poetry kept it alive after ordinary speech moved on.
senses.whyCN: 在 girl 和 woman 成为日常用词之前，maid 就是称呼年轻未婚女性的普通说法；日常口语改换之后，诗歌仍把它保留下来。

senses.title: A bride's attendant
senses.definition: a woman, usually unmarried, who attends a bride at her wedding
senses.definitionCN: 在婚礼上陪伴新娘的女性，通常为未婚女子
senses.example: She asked her younger sister to be her maid at the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 她请妹妹在婚礼上做她的女傧相。
senses.why: Wedding attendants were traditionally unmarried young women, so the old sense of a young woman survived in the wedding role long after the everyday sense faded.
senses.whyCN: 婚礼上的伴娘传统上由未婚年轻女子担任，因此「年轻女子」这个旧义在婚礼角色里保留了下来，比日常义项消失得晚得多。

intro.en: Maid is a Germanic word for a young unmarried woman that was shortened in Middle English and then narrowed to household service.
intro.cn: maid 是日耳曼语中表示年轻未婚女子的词，在中古英语里被缩短，随后词义收窄到家务服务。

items.en: The form mægden was a diminutive of mægeth, a word for a girl or virgin, and it named a young unmarried woman.
items.cn: 形式 mægden 是 mægeth（少女、处女的词）的指小形式，用来指年轻的未婚女子。

items.en: The reconstructed base *magadiz meant a young person, and it is also behind German Magd and Mädchen.
items.cn: 重构词根 *magadiz 意为年轻人，德语 Magd 与 Mädchen 也出自这里。

items.en: Middle English shortened maiden to maide, and the shorter form maid came to be used for household servants.
items.cn: 中古英语把 maiden 缩短为 maide，较短的 maid 开始被用来指家中仆役。

items.en: In wealthy households maid settled into the meaning of a female servant, while the older sense survived in ballads and in titles.
items.cn: 在富裕家庭里，maid 固定为女性仆人的意思，而较旧的「少女」义则在歌谣和称谓中留存。

items.en: Modern English uses maid mainly for domestic workers and in fixed phrases such as 「maid of honour」, with the literary sense marked as old-fashioned.
items.cn: 现代英语里 maid 主要用于家政工人和「maid of honour」这类固定短语，文学义则标为过时。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and compounds built on the same Germanic word; the near-meaning group gathers words for household service and helping roles.
note.cn: 形近组收同一日耳曼词上的形式与复合词；近义组收家务服务与协助角色的词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a shortened Germanic term for a young woman that moved from the girl herself to the work she did indoors.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是日耳曼语中「年轻女子」的缩略形式，词义从女子本人转移到她在室内做的活。

normal.en: Maid is the short form of maiden, so the two words share one history: first a young woman, then a woman who works indoors.
normal.cn: maid 是 maiden 的缩略形式，两个词共用一段历史：先指年轻女子，再指在室内干活的女性。

normal.en: The -en in maiden is an old diminutive ending, so maiden once meant a little young woman.
normal.cn: maiden 里的 -en 是古老的指小词尾，所以 maiden 原先指「小小的年轻女子」。

normal.en: Old English mægden and mægeth are related, and both point to an unmarried girl rather than to a job.
normal.cn: 古英语 mægden 与 mægeth 同源，两者都指向未婚少女，而不是某种职业。

normal.en: Barmaid joins bar and maid, keeping the old pattern of naming a woman by the place where she serves.
normal.cn: barmaid 由 bar 与 maid 合成，保留了「按服务场所称呼女性」的旧构词方式。

normal.en: Maid of honour is fixed as a wedding title, which is why the literary sense of maid still sounds natural there.
normal.cn: maid of honour 是固定的婚礼称谓，所以 maid 的文学义在那里听起来仍然自然。

abstract.en: A white apron by the kitchen door is enough to summon the whole history of the word: a girl, a household, a job.
abstract.cn: 厨房门边一条白围裙，就足以唤起这个词的全部历史：少女、家庭、一份工作。

abstract.en: The same word can wait by a river in a ballad and polish brass in a hallway, because both pictures begin with a young woman.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以在歌谣里于河边等候，也可以在门厅擦铜器，因为两幅画面都从一位年轻女子开始。

abstract.en: When a role outlives its everyday meaning, the old sense survives in ceremony, and maid of honour is that survival.
abstract.cn: 当某个角色比它的日常词义活得更久，旧义就留存在仪式里，maid of honour 正是这种留存。

definition_en: the act or sound of laughing
core_image: 一群人的笑声同时从屋里涌出来，像一阵轻快的风
scene: 客厅里有人讲了个笨拙的笑话，满屋的人一起笑出声。 Her laughter filled the small kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里是「笑声」（第 1 个义项：笑的声音或行为）；句意为她的笑声充满了小厨房。图中可辨识物件：客厅、围坐的人、冒着热气的杯子。

derivatives.zh: laughter 的词根动词，义为「笑；笑声」
由 laugh 加 -able 构成，义为「可笑的；荒唐的」
由 laugh 加 -ing 构成，义为「笑着的；带笑的」

senses.title: The sound of laughing
senses.definition: the sound made when people laugh, often heard as a whole rather than word by word
senses.definitionCN: 人们笑时发出的声音，通常作为一个整体被听见
senses.example: Her laughter filled the small kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她的笑声充满了小厨房。
senses.why: Laughter is the old noun beside the verb laugh; it names the sound itself, the way thunder names the noise rather than the flash.
senses.whyCN: laughter 是动词 laugh 旁边的古老名词，指声音本身，就像 thunder 指雷声而不是闪电。

senses.title: Amusement shown by laughing
senses.definition: the expression of amusement or joy through laughing, considered as a shared response
senses.definitionCN: 通过笑表现出来的愉悦或快乐，被视为一种共同的反应
senses.example: The room was full of laughter after the story.
senses.exampleCN: 故事讲完后，屋里满是欢笑。
senses.why: Because laughter is heard, it can stand for the whole mood of a group, not only for one person's sound.
senses.whyCN: 因为笑声是听得见的，它能代表一群人的整体气氛，而不只是某一个人的声音。

intro.en: Laughter is an Old English noun built beside the verb laugh, and the pair has stayed together for a thousand years.
intro.cn: laughter 是古英语中与动词 laugh 并列构成的名词，这一对词已经一起走了一千年。

items.en: Hleahter was the noun for laughter, formed from the verb hliehhan.
items.cn: hleahter 是表示「笑」的名词，由动词 hliehhan 构成。

items.en: The Germanic root also gives German lachen and Dutch lachen, all meaning to laugh.
items.cn: 同一日耳曼词根也给出德语 lachen 与荷兰语 lachen，都表示「笑」。

items.en: Middle English laughter keeps the noun while the verb settles into laugh.
items.cn: 中古英语保留名词 laughter，而动词固定为 laugh。

items.en: The spelling with -gh- becomes standard, matching the verb in the same period.
items.cn: 带 -gh- 的拼写在十六世纪成为标准，与同一时期的动词拼写一致。

items.en: Modern English keeps laughter almost unchanged, often in fixed phrases such as burst into laughter.
items.cn: 现代英语中 laughter 几乎未变，常出现在 burst into laughter 这样的固定短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the laugh family; the near-meaning group gathers sounds and moods of amusement.
note.cn: 形近组收 laugh 词族；近义组收表示愉快声音与情绪的词。

entries.definition: To make the sound of amusement, or that sound.

entries.definition: A light, silly laugh.

entries.definition: A quiet laugh with the mouth closed.

entries.definition: Great amusement expressed in laughter.

entries.definition: The feeling of finding something funny.

normalIntro.en: The noun is inseparable from its verb, and its suffix is the old -ter that turns an action into a thing heard.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词与它的动词不可分割，后缀是古老的 -ter，把动作变成听得见的东西。

normal.en: Laughter is the noun beside the verb laugh, not a separate word.
normal.cn: laughter 是动词 laugh 旁边的名词，不是另一个词。

normal.en: The ending -ter appears in other old nouns of action, such as laughter and slaughter.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ter 也出现在其他古老的动作名词里，如 laughter 与 slaughter。

normal.en: Burst into laughter is the common phrase for a sudden start.
normal.cn: burst into laughter 是表示「突然笑出声」的常用搭配。

normal.en: Laughter is uncountable: a burst of laughter, not a laughter.
normal.cn: laughter 不可数：说 a burst of laughter，不说 a laughter。

normal.en: The -gh- is silent, just as in laugh.
normal.cn: 其中的 -gh- 不发音，和 laugh 一样。

abstract.en: A sound can become a noun and then stand for a whole mood, which is how laughter fills a room.
abstract.cn: 一种声音可以变成名词，再代表一整个气氛，laughter 就是这样「充满」一个房间的。

abstract.en: English keeps both laugh and laughter so that the act and the sound can be named separately.
abstract.cn: 英语同时保留 laugh 与 laughter，让动作与声音可以分开命名。

abstract.en: Laughter is shared by definition: it is made to be heard.
abstract.cn: laughter 天生是共享的：它被制造出来就是为了让人听见。

branches.en: one sound that becomes the whole room
branches.cn: 一种声音变成整个房间

intro.en: An Old English noun, its verb, and the old suffix -ter make the core of this small family.
intro.cn: 一个古英语名词、它的动词，以及古老的后缀 -ter 构成这个小词族的核心。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to make the sound of amusement
an action made into a thing
items.meaningCN: 把动作变成名词的词尾

definition_zh: 田径运动；竞技体育；体育课（学科）
definition_en: sports such as running, jumping and throwing, especially track and field events
core_image: 红色跑道上发令枪冒烟，选手们冲出起跑线
scene: 校园运动会的广播里说： She won gold in athletics by breaking the school record in the hundred meters.
sceneCN: 这里指「田径运动」（第 1 个义项：跑、跳、投等项目）；句意为她在田径比赛中打破百米校纪录夺得金牌。

pos.zh: 田径运动；竞技体育；体育（学科，作单数）

derivatives.zh: 运动员
运动的；健壮的
健壮地；运动地

senses.title: Track and field sports
senses.definition: the group of sports including running, jumping, throwing and walking events
senses.definitionCN: 包括跑、跳、投、竞走等项目的运动总称
senses.example: She takes part in athletics every weekend during the season.
senses.exampleCN: 赛季期间她每周末都参加田径运动。
senses.why: British English groups all track and field events under one plural-looking name, athletics.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语把所有田径项目归到一个带 -s 的名称之下：athletics。

senses.title: Competitive sports in general
senses.definition: organized competitive sports at a school, college or national level
senses.definitionCN: 学校、大学或国家层面组织的竞技体育活动
senses.example: The university invests heavily in its athletics program.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学在竞技体育项目上投入巨大。
senses.why: Especially in American English, athletics widens from track events to the whole sports program.
senses.whyCN: 尤其在美式英语里，athletics 从田径扩展到整个体育项目体系。

senses.title: Physical exercise as a study or practice
senses.titleCN: 作为学科或实践的体育
senses.definition: the study or practice of physical exercise and training
senses.definitionCN: 对体育锻炼与训练的研究或实践
senses.example: He studied athletics and coaching at the sports institute.
senses.exampleCN: 他在体育学院学习体育学与教练课程。
senses.why: As a singular academic subject, athletics names the field of knowledge about sport.
senses.whyCN: 作单数的学科名称时，athletics 指关于体育的知识领域。

intro.en: athletics is the English plural-style noun from athletic, on Greek athlon (contest), referring to the whole set of contests.
intro.cn: athletics 是由 athletic 构成的带 -s 形式的英语名词，源自希腊语 athlon（竞赛），指整套竞技项目。

items.en: Greek athlon meant 'contest, prize'; athletes meant prize contestant.
items.cn: 希腊语 athlon 意为「竞赛、奖赏」；athletes 指争夺奖赏的选手。

items.en: Latin athleta kept the competitor sense in public games.
items.cn: 拉丁语 athleta 保留了公开竞技选手的含义。

items.en: English athletics appeared in the 17th century for the exercises and contests of ancient athletes.
items.cn: 英语 athletics 于 17 世纪出现，指古代竞技者的操练与比赛。

items.en: In the 19th century, athletics became the standard British name for track and field sports.
items.cn: 19 世纪维多利亚时代，athletics 成为英式田径运动的标准名称。

items.en: In American English, athletics broadened to mean the entire competitive sports program of an institution.
items.cn: 美式英语中，athletics 扩展为指机构整体的竞技体育项目。

note.en: Group one collects the same-root athl- family; group two collects near-meaning sports nouns.
note.cn: 第一组是同属 athl- 词根的词族；第二组是语义相近的体育类名词。

entries.definition: The individual competitor; athletics is the set of sports they compete in.
entries.definitionCN: 参赛的个人；athletics 是他们所参加的运动总称。

entries.definition: The adjective without -s; describes bodies, shoes and programs.
entries.definitionCN: 不带 -s 的形容词；形容体格、运动鞋与体育项目。

entries.definition: Ends in -ics like athletics but means balancing and tumbling acts, a different sport family.
entries.definitionCN: 与 athletics 同以 -ics 结尾，但指平衡与翻腾技巧，属不同运动门类。

entries.definition: The American name for the same running, jumping and throwing events.
entries.definitionCN: 美式对同一批跑、跳、投项目的称呼。

entries.definition: Any single game or physical contest; athletics is the collective field.
entries.definitionCN: 任一单项运动；athletics 是运动的总领域。

entries.definition: Another -ics sport name, focused on apparatus and floor exercises.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个 -ics 运动名，专注器械与自由体操。

normalIntro.en: athletics is athletic + -s: the whole family of athletic contests under one name.
normalIntro.cn: athletics 是 athletic + -s：把所有竞技项目收进一个名字。

normal.en: athlete lives inside it: athletics is what athletes do.
normal.cn: 词里有 athlete：athletics 就是运动员做的事。

normal.en: It looks plural but takes a singular verb: athletics is popular.
normal.cn: 形式像复数但谓语用单数：athletics is popular。

normal.en: British athletics equals American track and field.
normal.cn: 英式 athletics 相当于美式 track and field。

normal.en: -ics endings often name fields: physics, economics, athletics.
normal.cn: -ics 结尾常表学科领域：physics、economics、athletics。

normal.en: Picture a stadium with running track, jumping pits and throwing circles.
normal.cn: 想象一座有跑道、沙坑和投掷圈的体育场。

abstract.en: The smell of fresh-cut grass and rubber track on a summer meet day.
abstract.cn: 夏季赛事日，新割的青草与塑胶跑道混合的气味。

abstract.en: A starting gun's echo hanging over a silent stadium.
abstract.cn: 发令枪的回声悬在安静的体育场上空。

abstract.en: Lane numbers painted white on red rubber, straight ahead.
abstract.cn: 红色跑道上白色的道次编号，笔直向前。

examples.en: Athletics has been part of every modern Olympic Games since 1896.
examples.cn: 自 1896 年起，田径一直是每届现代奥运会的项目。

examples.en: The school's athletics day brings together all the track events.
examples.cn: 学校的运动会把所有田径项目聚在一起。

examples.en: He broke two national athletics records in one season.
examples.cn: 他一个赛季打破了两项全国田径纪录。

dict_mnemonic.text: athletic（运动的）+ -s（集合）= 各类竞技运动的总称 = 田径运动

root: 希腊语 athlon（竞赛、奖赏）→ athletes → athletic → + -s → athletics。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses widen out from one stadium image: track and field as a set, competitive sports as a program, and exercise as a field of study.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项由体育场这一画面展开：作为项目集合的田径、作为项目体系的竞技体育、作为研究领域的体育学。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red running track where runners, jumpers and throwers all compete.
core.cn: 核心意象：红色跑道上，跑者、跳者、投掷者同场竞技。

branches.en: TRACK AND FIELD: running, jumping and throwing as one named set.
branches.cn: 田径：跑、跳、投构成的总称。

branches.en: SPORTS PROGRAMS: the competitive system of a school or nation.
branches.cn: 体育项目体系：学校或国家的竞技体系。

branches.en: STUDY: physical training as an academic subject.
branches.cn: 学科：作为研究对象的体育训练。

branches.en: COMPETITION: from school meets to national championships.
branches.cn: 竞赛：从校运会到全国锦标赛。

branches.en: ORGANIZATION: the people and institutions that run sports.
branches.cn: 组织：管理体育的人与机构。

intro.en: athletics adds the collective -s to athletic; the athl- root (contest) also builds athlete, biathlon and decathlon.
intro.cn: athletics 在 athletic 上加集合性的 -s；athl- 词根（竞赛）还构成 athlete、biathlon、decathlon。

latinIntro.en: athl- is Greek for contest, passed through Latin athleta into modern sports vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: athl- 是希腊语的「竞赛」，经拉丁语 athleta 进入现代体育词汇。

definition_zh: 核实；证实；查证；验证（身份、数据、真伪）
definition_en: to check or prove that something is true, accurate or genuine
core_image: 一只手把证据和账本逐条核对，最后在末尾打上勾
scene: 门卫拦下访客，让他出示证件，又对着名单一个字母一个字母地核对。 The guard verified her name against the list before opening the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 verify 是「核实、查证」（第 1 个义项：检查某事是否真实准确）；句意为门卫开门前对照名单核实了她的名字。逐条核对再打勾的动作，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：核实、查证；证实；验证

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ication 构成，义为「核实；验证」
加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可核实的；可验证的」
由过去分词转为形容词，义为「已核实的；经验证的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「核实者；校验器」

senses.title: To check the facts
senses.titleCN: 核实：检查事实是否正确
senses.definition: to check that information is true or accurate
senses.definitionCN: 检查信息是否真实、准确
senses.example: Please verify the figures before the report goes out.
senses.exampleCN: 报告发布之前请核实这些数字。
senses.why: Latin verus means true and facere means to make; to verify is to make a thing true in the sense of proving it so.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 verus 意为「真」，facere 意为「做」；verify 就是通过证明来把一件事确立为真。

senses.title: To confirm with evidence
senses.definition: to establish the truth of something by presenting evidence
senses.definitionCN: 通过出示证据来确立某事的真实性
senses.example: Two independent witnesses verified his account.
senses.exampleCN: 两名独立证人证实了他的说法。
senses.why: Checking becomes proving when evidence is laid beside the claim, as one pan of a balance beside the other.
senses.whyCN: 当证据被摆在说法一旁，如同天平两边相对，核对就变成了证实。

senses.title: To confirm identity
senses.titleCN: 核验身份：确认是不是本人
senses.definition: to establish that a person or document is genuine, as with a passport or password
senses.definitionCN: 确认某个人或证件真实无误，如查验护照或密码
senses.example: Banks must verify the identity of every new customer.
senses.exampleCN: 银行必须核验每一位新客户的身份。
senses.why: A person can be 'true' too: the same test applies to who someone is, not only to what a claim says.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以是「真的」：同一套检验既用于一句话是否属实，也用于一个人是谁。

senses.title: To test a system or figure
senses.titleCN: 验证：检验数据或系统是否成立
senses.definition: to test a result, calculation or system to show that it works as claimed
senses.definitionCN: 检验结果、计算或系统是否如所称那样运行
senses.example: The engineers verified the bridge design with a computer model.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用计算机模型验证了桥梁设计。
senses.why: Here the truth under test is a working thing, and the test produces the proof.
senses.whyCN: 此时受检验的「真」是一件能运转的东西，而检验本身就产出了证明。

senses.title: As in verified accounts
senses.definition: used adjectivally in phrases such as a verified account, meaning officially confirmed
senses.definitionCN: 以形容词形式用于 verified account「已认证账号」等说法，意为经官方确认的
senses.example: Her verified account carries a small blue badge.
senses.exampleCN: 她的已认证账号上带着一个小小的蓝色标记。
senses.why: The act becomes a state: once the check is done, the mark stays on the thing.
senses.whyCN: 动作变成了状态：核对一旦完成，标记就留在那件东西上。

intro.en: Verify joins two Latin words, verus 'true' and facere 'to make', and the pair travelled through French into English.
intro.cn: verify 由两个拉丁词合成：verus「真」与 facere「做」，这一组合经法语进入英语。

items.en: The adjective verus meant 'true, real, genuine', and it also gave veritas 'truth'.
items.cn: 形容词 verus 意为「真的、真实的」，它还生出 veritas「真理」。

items.en: The verb facere meant 'to make, do', the source of dozens of English -fy verbs.
items.cn: 动词 facere 意为「做、造」，是英语许多以 -fy 结尾动词的来源。

items.en: Verificare meant 'to make true, prove to be true'; the medieval form is documented, though its first use is uncertain.
items.cn: verificare 意为「使成真、证明为真」；这一中世纪形式有文献可查，但首见年代不确定。

items.en: Old French verifier carried the sense of proving or establishing a thing as true.
items.cn: 古法语 verifier 带有「证明或确立某事物为真」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed verify in the fourteenth century, first in legal and scholarly contexts.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 verify，最初多用于法律与学术语境。

items.en: Computing gave the word a technical life: to verify data, a signature or an account.
items.cn: 计算机领域赋予这个词技术生命：验证数据、签名或账号。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other Latin -ficare verbs; the near-meaning group gathers ways of checking and confirming.
note.cn: 形近组收其他拉丁语 -ficare 动词；近义组收各种核对与确认的说法。

entries.definition: To make something clear; clarus 'clear' plus facere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「澄清」，由 clarus「清楚」加 facere 构成。

entries.definition: To confirm officially in writing; certus 'sure' plus facere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证明、颁发证书」，由 certus「确定」加 facere 构成。

entries.definition: To recognise or establish who or what something is.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「识别、确认身份」。

entries.definition: The noun of checking that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「核实、验证」。

entries.definition: To state that something is certainly true, often after being asked.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「确认」，常在被询问之后表示某事确实如此。

entries.definition: To look at something quickly to see whether it is right; the everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「检查」，是最日常的说法。

entries.definition: To prove something is valid or acceptable, especially by official test.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使生效、验证有效」，多指经过正式检验。

entries.definition: To support a claim with evidence; formal and heavy.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证实、用证据支持」，语气正式而厚重。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two real Latin parts, verus and facere, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语两部件 verus 与 facere，以及这个词出现的短语。

normal.en: veri- is true and -fy is to make: verify is to make true by proof.
normal.cn: veri- 是真，-fy 是做：verify 就是靠证明把事做真。

normal.en: Verify comes before you trust; confirm often comes when someone asks.
normal.cn: verify 发生在你相信之前；confirm 多发生在有人问起时。

normal.en: Verification is the noun, verifiable the adjective: check, then the checkable quality.
normal.cn: verification 是名词，verifiable 是形容词：先核对，再谈可核对的性质。

normal.en: A verified account has passed the check and keeps the badge.
normal.cn: 已认证账号通过了核对，于是保留那个标记。

normal.en: Computers verify a password in milliseconds; a witness may take years.
normal.cn: 计算机毫秒之间校验密码，而一个证人可能要用好几年。

abstract.en: Picture two columns on a page: the claim on the left, the evidence on the right, and a tick when they line up.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸上两栏：左边是说法，右边是证据，两者对齐时打一个勾。

abstract.en: The word is built to make truth, not to find it: the act of proving is what creates the certainty.
abstract.cn: 这个词生来是要「造出」真，而不是「发现」真：证明这一动作本身造出了确定。

abstract.en: The same tick works for facts, for identity and for a design that must hold a bridge.
abstract.cn: 同一个勾适用于事实、身份，以及必须撑住一座桥的设计。

examples.en: Journalists must verify a story before publishing it.
examples.cn: 记者在发表报道之前必须核实。

examples.en: The software verifies your password each time you log in.
examples.cn: 每次登录时，软件都会校验你的密码。

examples.en: Officials could not verify the number of people in the camp.
examples.cn: 官员无法核实营地中的人数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「verify 为瑞发」——为瑞（veri）发一张证明，核料必须是真的：核实

root: 由拉丁语 verus「真的」与 facere「做、造」组合而成，中世纪拉丁语 verificare「证明为真」，经古法语 verifier 进入英语；同族词有 verity、verdict、clarify、certify。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of verify move from checking a fact, to proving it with evidence, to testing a person, a system, and finally the lasting mark of a passed check.
sensesIntro.cn: verify 的五个义项从核对事实，到用证据证实，再到检验一个人、一套系统，最后落在通过核验后留下的持久标记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two columns on a page, claim and evidence, with a tick where they meet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页纸上的两栏，说法与证据，在二者吻合处打一个勾。

branches.en: CHECK LINE: the eye runs down the list comparing each item.
branches.cn: 核对线：目光沿清单逐项比对。

branches.en: PROOF LINE: evidence is set beside the claim until the balance is level.
branches.cn: 证明线：把证据摆在说法旁边，直到天平持平。

branches.en: TEST LINE: a person or a system is put through the same test.
branches.cn: 检验线：人和系统都要经过同一套检验。

branches.en: MARK LINE: the finished check leaves a badge behind.
branches.cn: 标记线：核验完成后留下一个标记。

branches.en: CONTRAST: check looks, verify proves, confirm answers.
branches.cn: 对照线：check 是看，verify 是证明，confirm 是应声作答。

intro.en: Verify is a Latin compound: a true-root plus a make-root, closed by English endings.
intro.cn: verify 是拉丁语复合词：一个「真」词根加一个「做」词根，再以英语词尾收束。

latinIntro.en: Both Latin halves are documented: verus and facere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的两半都有文献可查：verus 与 facere。

items.example: It carries the idea of truth.

items.exampleCN: 它连接 verus 与 facere。
它构成 clarify 与 certify。

definition_en: to produce flowers
core_image: 枝头刚刚绽开的玫瑰
scene: 一夜之间，院里的玫瑰枝头全开了。 The roses bloom in early summer.
sceneCN: 这里 bloom 是「开花」（第 1 个义项：长出花朵）；句意是玫瑰在初夏开花。

pos.zh: 动词：开花；绽放；焕发光彩

derivatives.zh: 盛开的，正在开花的
语义关联词，义为「花朵」，与 bloom 同指树上开的花

senses.title: To produce flowers
senses.definition: to open into flowers
senses.definitionCN: 绽开成为花朵
senses.example: The roses bloom in early summer.
senses.exampleCN: 玫瑰在初夏开花。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, the opening of a flower.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，指花朵开放。

senses.title: A flower or the flowering state
senses.definition: a flower, or the period when plants flower
senses.definitionCN: 一朵花，或植物开花的时期
senses.example: The garden is in full bloom.
senses.exampleCN: 花园里花开正盛。
senses.why: The verb became a noun for the flower and its season.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为名词，指花朵与开花的时节。

senses.title: To grow healthy and confident
senses.definition: to develop in a healthy and confident way
senses.definitionCN: 健康而自信地成长发展
senses.example: She bloomed after moving to the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 搬到海边之后，她整个人焕发光彩。
senses.why: A person opening up was pictured like a flower opening.
senses.whyCN: 一个人舒展开来，被比作花朵绽开。

intro.en: Bloom came from Norse and named a flower before it named the act.
intro.cn: bloom 来自诺斯语，先指花朵，后指开花的动作。

items.en: blom meant a flower.
items.cn: blom 意为花。

items.en: blome entered English as bloom.
items.cn: blome 以 bloom 的形式进入英语。

items.en: bloom also meant the prime of life.
items.cn: bloom 也开始指人生的盛年。

items.en: bloom named a healthy glow on the face.
items.cn: bloom 指脸上健康的光泽。

items.en: bloom covers flowers and flourishing.
items.cn: 如今 bloom 兼指开花与兴旺。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the blo- opening; the near-meaning group names flowers and growth.
note.cn: 形近组都以 blo- 开头；近义组是花朵与生长类词。

entries.definition: to send out air
entries.definitionCN: 吹

entries.definition: the red liquid in the body
entries.definitionCN: 血

normalIntro.en: Bloom is the moment a bud decides to open.
normalIntro.cn: bloom 是花苞决定张开的那一瞬间。

normal.en: In full bloom means flowering completely.
normal.cn: in full bloom 表示花开到最盛。

normal.en: Bloom works as both verb and noun.
normal.cn: bloom 既可作动词也可作名词。

normal.en: Blossom is close in meaning.
normal.cn: blossom 与它意思接近。

normal.en: The plural adds s.

normal.en: The double o looks like two buds.
normal.cn: 其中的双 o 像两个并排的花苞。

abstract.en: See roses opening overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象玫瑰一夜之间开放。

abstract.en: See bees moving between petals.
abstract.cn: 想象蜜蜂在花瓣间穿行。

abstract.en: See a shy person suddenly laughing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个腼腆的人忽然笑开。

examples.en: The roses bloom in early summer.
examples.cn: 玫瑰在初夏开花。

examples.en: The garden is in full bloom.
examples.cn: 花园里花开正盛。

examples.en: She bloomed after moving to the coast.
examples.cn: 搬到海边之后，她整个人焕发光彩。

dict_mnemonic.text: bloom 里的双 o 像两朵并排的小花，看到双 o 就想到开花。

root: bloom 源自古诺斯语 blom（花），中古英语进入英语后先指花朵，再指开花的动作，十六世纪起又引申为人生的盛年与脸上的光泽。

sensesIntro.en: A flower opens, a garden flowers, and a person flourishes.
sensesIntro.cn: 一朵花开、一园花放、一个人焕发光彩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rose opening on a branch overnight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一夜之间枝头绽开的玫瑰。

branches.en: roses bloom
branches.cn: 玫瑰开花

branches.en: in full bloom
branches.cn: 盛开

branches.cn: 春季花期

branches.cn: 因健康而容光焕发

intro.en: Bloom takes -ing for an adjective and shares a family with blossom.
intro.cn: bloom 加 -ing 构成形容词，并与 blossom 同族。

definition_zh: 发明；发明物；编造；创造力
definition_en: the act of creating something new, the thing created, or something made up rather than true
core_image: 桌上散着齿轮、绳子和纸片，忽然拼成一个会转的小装置
scene: 车库里堆满拆开的零件，一个人把最后一根线接上，机器嗡嗡转了起来。 The telephone was not one person's invention alone.
sceneCN: 这里 invention 是「发明」（第 1 个义项：创造新事物这件事），句意为电话并非某一个人的发明。画面里的物件：齿轮、线圈、工作台。

pos.zh: 名词：发明；发明物；编造；创造力

collocations.phrase: necessity is the mother of invention

derivatives.zh: 去后缀构成，义为「发明；编造」
由 invent 加 -or 构成，义为「发明者」
由 invent 加 -ive 构成，义为「有创造力的」
形近同源词，义为「清单；存货」

senses.title: The act of creating
senses.titleCN: 把新东西造出来的那件事
senses.definition: the act of designing and making something that did not exist before
senses.definitionCN: 设计并制造出此前并不存在之物的行为
senses.example: The invention of the wheel changed travel for ever.
senses.exampleCN: 车轮的发明永远改变了出行。
senses.why: Latin invenire meant to come upon; an invention is something found by searching.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 invenire 意为「碰上、发现」，invention 是找出来的东西。

senses.title: The thing created
senses.definition: a device, process, or idea that someone has created
senses.definitionCN: 由某人创造出来的器具、方法或想法
senses.example: Her latest invention folds into the size of a book.
senses.exampleCN: 她最新的发明能折成一本书那么大。
senses.why: The noun points at the object as easily as at the act.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能指行为，也能直接指向那个物件。

senses.title: Something made up
senses.definition: a story or claim that is false and deliberately created
senses.definitionCN: 故意编造出来的虚假说法或故事
senses.example: The whole interview, he said, was an invention.
senses.exampleCN: 他说那篇采访整篇都是编造的。
senses.why: If inventing means making from nothing, a lie is an invention too.
senses.whyCN: 如果发明就是从无到有，那么谎言也是一种发明。

senses.title: Creative power
senses.definition: the ability to think of new things and make them
senses.definitionCN: 想出并做出新事物的能力
senses.example: The job calls for invention more than routine.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作靠的是创造力，而不是按部就班。
senses.why: The abstract sense names the faculty rather than any one product.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义指的是这种能力，而不是某件产品。

intro.en: Invention comes from Latin invenire, to come upon something by searching.
intro.cn: invention 来自拉丁语 invenire，意为通过寻找而碰上某物。

items.en: Venire meant to come; in- meant into or upon.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，in- 意为「进入、朝向」。

items.en: Invenire meant to find or to come across.
items.cn: invenire 意为找到或偶然碰上。

items.en: Inventio named the finding, later the making of something new.
items.cn: inventio 指「找到」，后来指造出新东西。

items.en: French invention kept both finding and devising.
items.cn: 法语 invention 兼有「发现」与「设计」。

items.en: English used invention for machines, stories, and talent.
items.cn: 英语用 invention 指机器、故事与才能。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vent- coming stem; the near-meaning group holds words for new creations.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -vent-「来」词干；近义组收表示新造之物的词。

entries.definition: The verb of creating something new.
entries.definitionCN: 动词义为「发明」。

entries.definition: The person who creates it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「发明者」。

entries.definition: A coming between, from the same venire.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「干预」，同出 venire。

entries.definition: Finding something that already existed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「发现」，对象本已存在。

entries.definition: Bringing something into being, often artistic.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「创造」，偏艺术。

entries.definition: A machine made for a particular purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「装置」，是发明的实物形态。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the picture of parts coming together into something that works.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子守着「零件拼成一件能转起来的东西」的画面。

normal.en: Invention is invent plus -ion, the act made into a thing.
normal.cn: invention 是 invent 加 -ion，动作变成了东西。

normal.en: The same venire is inside intervention and event.
normal.cn: 同一个 venire 也在 intervention 与 event 里。

normal.en: To invent can also mean to make up a story.
normal.cn: to invent 也可以指编故事。

normal.en: A patent protects an invention, not an idea in the air.
normal.cn: 专利保护的是发明，而不是空中的念头。

normal.en: The proverb says need is the mother of invention.
normal.cn: 谚语说，需要是发明之母。

abstract.en: An invention is an argument with the world that ends in a tool.
abstract.cn: 发明是一场与世界的争论，最后落成一件工具。

abstract.en: Finding and making share one Latin word for a reason.
abstract.cn: 发现与制造共用一个拉丁词，自有道理。

abstract.en: Every lie is a small invention with no patent.
abstract.cn: 每个谎言都是一项没申请专利的小发明。

examples.en: The invention of the printing press made books cheap.
examples.cn: 印刷机的发明让书变便宜了。

examples.en: The story about the ghost was pure invention.
examples.cn: 关于鬼的那个故事纯属编造。

examples.en: Her job rewards invention rather than obedience.
examples.cn: 她的工作看重创造力，而不是听话。

dict_mnemonic.text: invent（发明）+ ion（名词）——新造出来的东西

root: 拉丁语 venire「来」→ invenire「碰上、找到」→ inventio「发现、创制」→ 古法语 → 英语 invention。同族有 invent、inventor、inventory。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: the act of creating, the thing created, a deliberate lie, and inventive power.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：创造这一行为、造出来的东西、故意编造，以及创造的能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose parts on a bench suddenly moving together as a machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：工作台上散着的零件忽然合成一台转动的机器。

branches.en: THE WORKBENCH: the act of designing something new.
branches.cn: 工作台这条线：设计新东西的过程。

branches.en: THE DEVICE: the object that resulted.
branches.cn: 装置这条线：最终得到的那件东西。

branches.en: THE TALE: a story invented out of nothing.
branches.cn: 故事这条线：从无中生出的说法。

branches.en: THE MIND: the talent for finding new ways.
branches.cn: 头脑这条线：找到新办法的才能。

branches.en: THE LINK: act and object wear the same name.
branches.cn: 连接线：行为与物件共用同一个名字。

intro.en: Invention is in- plus the root vent- "come" and the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: invention 由 in- 加词根 vent-「来」与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin invenire and inventio are recorded forms of the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 invenire 与 inventio 是同一族的记载形式。

items.example: The root also appears in event and prevent.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 event 与 prevent。

items.example: The verb is the direct source.
The noun gives the abstract sense.

items.meaning: a list of what is found
items.example: It keeps the older finding sense.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了更早的「找到」义。

definition_en: to remove something completely; to defeat and remove from a competition; to rule out; to kill
core_image: 把碍事的东西一件件扫出门槛之外
scene: 清洁队把仓库角落的废弃物全部清走。 The crew eliminated every trace of waste before the inspection.
sceneCN: 这里 eliminate 是「彻底清除」（第 01 个义项：把某物完全去掉）；句意是检查前工人清掉了所有废弃物痕迹。

pos.zh: 及物动词：消除；排除；淘汰；清除

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ion 构成，义为「消除；淘汰」
由动词加 -or 构成，义为「消除者；淘汰赛」
由动词加 -able 构成，义为「可消除的」

senses.title: To remove something completely
senses.definition: to get rid of something completely, especially something unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 把不想要的东西完全去掉
senses.example: The crew eliminated every trace of waste before the inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 检查前工人清掉了所有废弃物的痕迹。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to turn something out of doors, with limen as the threshold, so the core picture is putting an unwanted thing outside the house.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语原义是「赶出门外」，limen 就是门槛，所以核心画面是把不想要的东西放到屋外。

senses.title: To knock a team out of a contest
senses.definition: to defeat a player or team so that they leave a competition
senses.definitionCN: 击败选手或队伍，使其离开比赛
senses.example: Our team was eliminated in the first round.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队在第一轮就被淘汰了。
senses.why: A losing side is pushed out of the tournament the way a thing is pushed out of the door, so the same verb describes sporting removal.
senses.whyCN: 输掉的一方被挤出赛事，就像东西被赶出门外，于是同一个动词也用来描述赛场上的出局。

senses.title: To rule something out
senses.definition: to show that something is not possible or not involved
senses.definitionCN: 证明某事不可能或与某事无关
senses.example: The police eliminated him as a suspect.
senses.exampleCN: 警方排除了他的嫌疑。
senses.why: When a suspect is cleared, that person is removed from the list of possibilities, which is again a mental clearing away.
senses.whyCN: 嫌疑人被洗清后，就从可能性名单里被拿掉了，这仍是一种思维上的清除。

senses.title: To kill, in formal use
senses.definition: to kill a person or animal, used in formal or euphemistic writing
senses.definitionCN: 杀死人或动物，用于正式或委婉的表达
senses.example: The disease eliminated entire herds.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病消灭了整群牲畜。
senses.why: The strongest form of removal is to take a life, so the verb stretches from clearing objects to clearing living things.
senses.whyCN: 最彻底的清除是夺走生命，于是这个动词从清理物品延伸到清除活物。

intro.en: Eliminate comes from Latin eliminare, to turn out of doors, built on limen, a threshold.
intro.cn: eliminate 出自拉丁语 eliminare，意为「赶出门外」，其根是 limen（门槛）。

items.en: Limen meant threshold or doorway, the line between inside and outside.
items.cn: limen 意为门槛、门口，是内与外之间的界线。

items.en: The verb eliminare meant to turn someone out of the house.
items.cn: 动词 eliminare 意为把人赶出屋外。

items.en: Its participle eliminatus carried the sense of having been put out.
items.cn: 其分词 eliminatus 带有「已被赶出去」的意思。

items.en: English borrowed the verb and widened it from people to things and ideas.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入该动词，并把对象从人扩大到事物与观念。

items.en: Sports, medicine and logic each took the word for their own kind of removal.
items.cn: 体育、医学与逻辑各自取用这个词，表达本领域的「去除」。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the elimination family; the near-meaning group separates ordinary removal, total destruction and exclusion.
note.cn: 形近组留在 elimination 词族内部；近义组区分一般去除、彻底根除与排除在外。

entries.definition: The act or result of removing something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「消除、淘汰」这一动作或结果。

entries.definition: One that removes, or a knockout match.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「消除者」或「淘汰赛」。

entries.definition: Able to be removed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可消除的」。

entries.definition: To take something away from a place, without necessarily destroying it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「移走、拿开」，不一定销毁。

entries.definition: To destroy something completely and root it out.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「根除」，强调连根拔起。

entries.definition: To keep someone or something out on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「排除在外」，强调不让进入。

entries.definition: To beat an opponent, though not always removing them from a contest.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「击败」，但不一定把对方淘汰出赛。

normalIntro.en: These hooks read eliminate as e- plus limen, out of the threshold, then follow the same push into sport, logic and medicine.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把 eliminate 读成 e- 加 limen，即「推过门槛」，再让同一股推力走进赛场、推理与医学。

normal.en: E- means out and limen means threshold: push it out the door.
normal.cn: e- 表示向外，limen 是门槛：把它推出门。

normal.en: A filter eliminates dust by keeping it out.
normal.cn: 过滤器把灰尘挡在外面，就等于消除了灰尘。

normal.en: A knockout round eliminates the losing side.
normal.cn: 淘汰赛把输的一方送出赛事。

normal.en: Detectives eliminate suspects one by one.
normal.cn: 侦探把嫌疑人一个个排除。

normal.en: Elimination is the noun built with -ion.
normal.cn: elimination 是加 -ion 构成的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a broom sweeping things over a threshold and out.
abstract.cn: 想象一把扫帚把东西扫过门槛、扫到外面。

abstract.en: Every sense is a list getting shorter.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都像一份名单在变短。

abstract.en: The word removes objects, rivals, doubts and lives.
abstract.cn: 这个词能移除物品、对手、疑虑，甚至生命。

examples.en: The crew eliminated every trace of waste before the inspection.
examples.cn: 检查前工人清掉了所有废弃物的痕迹。

examples.en: Our team was eliminated in the first round.
examples.cn: 我们队在第一轮就被淘汰了。

examples.en: The police eliminated him as a suspect.
examples.cn: 警方排除了他的嫌疑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一个里面没内特」——里面没东西了，就是被清空、被消除

root: 拉丁语 eliminare，由 e-（出）加 limen（门槛）构成，字面为「赶出门外」；引申为清除、排除与淘汰。

sensesIntro.en: Eliminate starts with clearing an object out of the house, then clears a team from a contest, a person from suspicion and finally a life from the world.
sensesIntro.cn: eliminate 从把物品清出屋外开始，继而把队伍清出赛事、把某人清出嫌疑名单，最后把生命清出世界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing an unwanted thing over the threshold and out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把不想要的东西推过门槛、推到门外。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: waste and errors cleared away.
branches.cn: 物品线：废弃物与错误被清理掉。

branches.en: THE CONTEST: the losing side sent home.
branches.cn: 赛事线：输掉的一方被送回家。

branches.en: THE LIST: a suspect taken off the board.
branches.cn: 名单线：嫌疑人被从板上拿掉。

branches.en: THE LIFE: living things cleared from the world.
branches.cn: 生命线：活物被从世上清除。

branches.en: ONE PUSH: object, rival and doubt all leave the same door.
branches.cn: 同一推：物品、对手与疑虑走的是同一扇门。

intro.en: Eliminate is built from the prefix e-, the root limen and the verb ending -ate; its derivatives then add -ion, -or and -able.
intro.cn: eliminate 由前缀 e-、词根 limen 与动词词尾 -ate 构成；派生词再加上 -ion、-or 与 -able。

latinIntro.en: Latin limen and eliminare are recorded; English added the familiar verb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 limen 与 eliminare 均有记录；英语又加上了常见的动词词尾。

definition_en: a signal that tells someone to begin, or the long stick used in billiards
core_image: 舞台侧幕里有人悄悄抬起手，演员立刻开口
scene: 舞台侧幕里一只手轻轻抬起，演员随即开口。 The light was her cue to walk on stage.
sceneCN: 这里 cue 指「提示」（第 1 个义项：示意某人开始动作或说话）；句意是灯光就是她上台的提示。

derivatives.zh: 提词卡
提示的动作

senses.title: A signal to act
senses.definition: a signal that tells someone to begin or to speak
senses.definitionCN: 示意某人开始或说话的信号
senses.example: The bell was our cue to leave.
senses.exampleCN: 铃声就是我们离开的信号。
senses.why: A small sign can set a whole action going.
senses.whyCN: 一个小小的信号，能带动一整套动作。

senses.title: A hint from others
senses.definition: a hint about what to do, taken from someone else
senses.definitionCN: 从别人那里得到的做法暗示
senses.example: He took his cue from the older players.
senses.exampleCN: 他照着年长球员的做法行事。
senses.why: We learn the next move by watching a neighbour.
senses.whyCN: 看着旁边的人，就学会了下一步。

senses.title: The stick in billiards
senses.definition: the long stick used to hit the ball in billiards
senses.definitionCN: 台球中用来击球的长杆
senses.example: She chalked her cue before the shot.
senses.exampleCN: 击球前她给球杆上了粉。
senses.why: A long wooden arm reaches where a hand cannot.
senses.whyCN: 一条木头长臂，伸到手够不到的地方。

intro.en: Cue may come from Latin quando, when, written in scripts to mark the moment an actor begins.
intro.cn: cue 可能出自拉丁语 quando（何时），写在剧本上标记演员开口的时刻。

items.en: Quando meant when, a word written in the margin of a script.
items.cn: quando 意为何时，常写在剧本页边。

items.en: Actors used the letter q for quando at the point of entry.
items.cn: 演员在入场处用字母 q 代表 quando。

items.en: Cue named the words just before an actor spoke.
items.cn: cue 指演员开口前的那几句词。

items.en: It widened to any signal that starts an action.
items.cn: 它扩展为任何启动动作的信号。

items.en: The billiard cue came separately from queue, a tail.
items.cn: 台球杆另出自法语 queue（尾巴）。

items.en: One spelling now covers a stage signal and a stick.
items.cn: 如今一个拼写既指舞台信号，也指球杆。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ue ending, and the meaning group names other signals that start something.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ue 结尾，近义组列出其他启动某事的信号。

entries.definition: a line of waiting people
entries.definitionCN: 排队等候的人

entries.definition: to make a sick person well
entries.definitionCN: 让病人康复

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a hand in the wings and end with a stick on green cloth.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从侧幕里的一只手开始，落到绿布上的一根杆。

normal.en: A cue is a small sign that starts a big action.
normal.cn: cue 是启动大动作的小信号。

normal.en: The letter q in the script means you speak now.
normal.cn: 剧本里的字母 q 就是轮到你说话。

normal.en: Watch others and take your cue from them.
normal.cn: 看着别人，从他们那里得到提示。

normal.en: Miss the cue and the scene moves on without you.
normal.cn: 错过提示，戏就把你落下往前走了。

normal.en: The same sound names a stick that starts a shot.
normal.cn: 同一个音也指启动一杆的球杆。

abstract.en: Picture a finger lifting in the dark wings.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗侧幕里一根手指抬起。

abstract.en: Picture an actor breathing in before the first line.
abstract.cn: 想象演员在开口前吸一口气。

abstract.en: Picture chalk dust on the tip of a cue.
abstract.cn: 想象球杆头上的一点粉。

examples.en: The teacher gave us a cue to begin.
examples.cn: 老师给了我们开始的提示。

examples.en: He took his cue from her silence and left.
examples.cn: 他从她的沉默里得到暗示，离开了。

examples.en: She laid the cue gently on the table.
examples.cn: 她把球杆轻轻放在桌上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cue 记成「该你了」：剧本边上一个字母 q，就是演员开口的时刻。

root: 可能出自拉丁语 quando（何时），剧本里以字母 q 标记演员开口之处；本义是开口前的提示词，后泛指任何启动动作的信号。台球杆一义另来自法语 queue（尾巴）。

sensesIntro.en: From a stage signal, to any borrowed hint, to the stick that starts a shot.
sensesIntro.cn: 从舞台信号，到任何借来的暗示，再到启动一杆的球杆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised in the wings, an actor stepping out.
core.cn: 核心意象：侧幕里一只手抬起，演员迈步出场。

branches.en: A signal tells a person that the moment has come.
branches.cn: 一个信号告诉人，时刻到了。

branches.en: A hint is a cue borrowed from someone else.
branches.cn: 暗示是从别人那里借来的提示。

branches.en: The stick carries the old meaning of a starting point.
branches.cn: 球杆保留着「起点」这层旧义。

branches.en: Both a stage signal and a borrowed hint push us forward.
branches.cn: 舞台信号与借来的暗示都推我们往前。

branches.en: Neither hint nor stick works without a hand to use it.
branches.cn: 暗示与球杆，都要有手来用才生效。

intro.en: Cue forms a small set of words for signals, prompts, and the tools of the game.
intro.cn: cue 组成一小族词，关于信号、提示与这项运动的器具。

latinIntro.en: The Latin quando, when, is the likely root under the stage sense of cue.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 quando（何时）可能是 cue 舞台义背后的根。

items.meaning: a card showing words to say

Cueing is done from the side.

derivatives.zh: 浸泡者；大雨
渗入量

senses.title: Leave in liquid
senses.definition: to leave something in liquid for a time
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放在液体中一段时间
senses.example: The beans soaked in water overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 豆子在水里浸泡了一夜。
senses.why: This is the central kitchen sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的厨房义项。

senses.title: Become very wet
senses.definition: to become completely wet
senses.definitionCN: 变得完全湿透
senses.example: The rain soaked through my coat.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水湿透了我的外套。
senses.why: Long exposure to liquid means being wet through.
senses.whyCN: 长时间接触液体意味着湿透。

senses.title: Absorb liquid
senses.definition: to take in liquid, often through a surface
senses.definitionCN: 常通过表面吸入液体
senses.example: The cloth soaked up the spilled milk.
senses.exampleCN: 布把洒出的牛奶吸干了。
senses.why: Soaking can move liquid into a material.
senses.whyCN: 浸泡能把液体吸进材料中。

senses.title: A long bath
senses.definition: a long relaxing bath
senses.definitionCN: 长时间放松的泡澡
senses.example: She had a long soak in the tub.
senses.exampleCN: 她在浴缸里泡了很久。
senses.why: The verb became a noun of relaxation.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为表示放松的名词。

intro.en: Soak comes from an Old English word meaning to steep.
intro.cn: soak 来自古英语中意为「浸泡」的词。

items.en: Socian meant to soak.

items.en: The word kept the sense of steeping.
items.cn: 这个词保留了浸泡的含义。

items.cn: 它意为湿透。

items.en: It meant to absorb liquid.

items.en: Soak up also means learn quickly.
items.cn: soak up 也意为快速学会。

note.en: Soak is compared with look-alike words and words for wetting or absorbing.
note.cn: 把 soak 与形近词以及表示浸湿或吸收的词作比较。

entries.definition: a soft covering for the foot

normalIntro.en: Soak is liquid moving slowly into something, or the time spent in it.
normalIntro.cn: soak 是液体慢慢进入某物，或泡在其中的时光。

normal.en: The beans soaked in water overnight.
normal.cn: 豆子在水里浸泡了一夜。

normal.en: The rain soaked through my coat.
normal.cn: 雨水湿透了我的外套。

normal.en: The cloth soaked up the spilled milk.
normal.cn: 布把洒出的牛奶吸干了。

normal.en: She had a long soak in the tub.
normal.cn: 她在浴缸里泡了很久。

normal.en: He soaks up new ideas quickly.
normal.cn: 他很快就能吸收新想法。

abstract.en: A mind soaks up what it stays near.
abstract.cn: 心智会吸收它长久接近的东西。

abstract.en: Give dry things time; water cannot be rushed in.
abstract.cn: 给干渴之物时间，水无法被催促着进入。

abstract.en: One long soak can undo a long day.
abstract.cn: 一次长时间的浸泡能消解漫长的一天。

examples.en: The beans soaked in water overnight.
examples.cn: 豆子在水里浸泡了一夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: soak 与 soap、sock 形近；soak up 是「吸收」，soaking wet 是「湿透了」。

root: 由古英语 socian（浸泡）演变而来，核心义「让液体慢慢进入」。

sensesIntro.en: Soak means to steep, become wet through, absorb liquid, or take a long bath.
sensesIntro.cn: soak 指浸泡、湿透、吸收液体，或长时间泡澡。

core.en: Liquid entering slowly and completely.
core.cn: 液体缓慢而彻底地进入。

branches.en: Beans rest in water.
branches.cn: 豆子静置在水中。

branches.en: Rain reaches through cloth.
branches.cn: 雨穿透衣物。

branches.en: Cloth pulls liquid inward.
branches.cn: 布把液体向内吸。

branches.en: A person rests in warm water.
branches.cn: 人在温水中休息。

branches.en: Steeping and absorbing are one process.
branches.cn: 浸泡与吸收是同一个过程。

intro.en: Soak builds words for wetting, absorption, and heavy rain.
intro.cn: soak 构成表示浸湿、吸收和豪雨的词。

latinIntro.en: Soak is a native English word, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: soak 是英语本族词，不是拉丁语。

items.example: Soak the rice for an hour.
The clothes are soaking in the tub.

items.example: We got caught in a soaker.
The soakage left a dark mark.
