definition_zh: 在…下画线；在…下面划线；强调；凸显
definition_en: to draw a line under a word or phrase, or to give special importance to something
core_image: 一支笔在纸上的字句下面压出一道笔直的横线，把这句话从纸面上抬起来
scene: 老师在黑板上写下一串生词，转身提醒全班把最难的那个词划出来。 She underlined the word twice so nobody would miss it.
sceneCN: 这里 underline 是「在…下画线」（第 1 个义项：在文字下方画出线条）；句意为她把这个词划了两遍，好让谁都不会漏掉。纸上被划出的那道横线，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ing 构成，义为「下划线；划线做法」
由同义近形词构成，义为「在…下划线；强调」
由本词加 -ed 构成，义为「划线的；带下划线的」

senses.title: A line drawn beneath words
senses.definition: to draw a straight line under a word or phrase, usually to mark it as important
senses.definitionCN: 在词或短语下面画一条直线，通常用来标记其重要性
senses.example: She underlined every new word in her notebook.
senses.exampleCN: 她把笔记本里每个生词都划了下划线。
senses.why: The prefix under- puts the line below, and line is the stroke itself; the word is almost a picture of what it does.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 under- 把线放在下面，line 就是那道笔画；这个词几乎把动作画了出来。

senses.title: To stress a point
senses.definition: to give special emphasis to an idea, fact, or statement when speaking or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在说话或写作时特别强调某个想法、事实或说法
senses.example: The report underlines the need for cleaner water in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 报告强调了这个村子需要更干净的水。
senses.why: An underlined sentence is one the reader must not skip; stressing a point does the same thing with the voice.
senses.whyCN: 划线句是读者不能跳过的一句；强调某点就是用声音做同样的事。

senses.title: A mark of emphasis
senses.definition: a line drawn under written or printed words as a mark of emphasis or of a link
senses.definitionCN: 在书写或印刷文字下方画出的线，用作强调标记或链接标记
senses.example: The teacher put a red underline under the misspelled name.
senses.exampleCN: 老师在拼错的名字下面画了一道红色下划线。
senses.why: The verb became a noun: the stroke itself is now a thing you can see and point at.
senses.whyCN: 动词转成了名词：那道笔画本身成了看得见、指得出的东西。

senses.title: Printed with a line below
senses.definition: printed or displayed with a line beneath the letters, as links and titles often are
senses.definitionCN: 字母下方带有线条地印刷或显示，网页链接与标题常如此
senses.example: In the old dictionary every headword appears underlined in bold.
senses.exampleCN: 在那本旧词典里，每个词目都以加粗并划下划线的方式出现。
senses.why: Here the word describes the look of the text rather than an act: the line is already there.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词描述的是文字的样子而不是动作：线已经在那里了。

senses.title: To make something stand out
senses.definition: to make a quality, problem, or difference more obvious, as if drawing a line under it
senses.definitionCN: 使某种性质、问题或差别更加明显，如同在其下面画线
senses.example: The empty seats underlined how few people had come.
senses.exampleCN: 空着的座位更凸显出到场的人有多么少。
senses.why: The image moves off the page: whatever is underlined stands out from everything around it.
senses.whyCN: 意象离开了纸面：被划线的东西总是从周围一切中凸显出来。

intro.en: Underline is a plain English compound, made of a preposition and a Latin loanword, and it is recorded only from the modern period.
intro.cn: underline 是朴素的英语复合词，由一个介词与一个拉丁语借词组成，直到近代才有记录。

items.en: The preposition under is native Old English under, meaning beneath or below.
items.cn: 介词 under 是本土的古英语 under，意为「在……之下」。

items.en: The noun linea meant a linen thread used as a plumb line, and from it a drawn line.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 linea 原指铅垂用的麻线，后指画出的线。

items.en: Line entered English through Old French ligne, so the two halves of the compound come from different layers.
items.cn: line 经由古法语 ligne 进入英语，因此这个复合词的两半来自不同层次。

items.en: English joined under and line to name a stroke drawn beneath writing; the verb follows the noun closely.
items.cn: 英语把 under 与 line 合起来，指写在文字下方的一道笔画；动词紧随名词出现。

items.en: Later the word was extended to emphasis in speech and to anything that stands out from its background.
items.cn: 后来这个词被扩展到言语中的强调，以及任何从背景中凸显出来的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other words built with under-; the near-meaning group gathers marking and stressing verbs with different tools.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 under- 构成的词；近义组收标记与强调的动词，所用手段各不相同。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning hidden beneath the surface but real and important.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「潜在的、根本的」，指藏在表面之下却真实重要。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning at a deeper or more basic level.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「从根本上、在更深层次上」。

entries.definition: A verb meaning to weaken something gradually from below.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「逐渐削弱、从根基上破坏」。

entries.definition: A noun or verb for the outer edge or a summary; it looks close but means the opposite kind of line.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「轮廓、概要」；拼写相近，但指的是另一种线。

entries.definition: A noun for material laid under a carpet or floor covering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「衬垫、地毯下面的垫层」。

entries.definition: To give special importance to something in speech or writing; it does not use a visible mark.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「强调」，用于言语或写作，不依赖可见的标记。

entries.definition: To mark text with colour or to draw attention to the most important part.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「用彩笔标出、突出」，多指用颜色而非线条。

entries.definition: To say a word or point with extra force, or to place emphasis on it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「强调；重读」，指用更大的力气说出某词或某点。

entries.definition: To make a feature more noticeable; more formal and often about appearance.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使突出、加剧」，较正式，常指外观上的特征。

entries.definition: A general verb for putting a sign on something; underline is one particular kind of mark.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「标记」，泛指做记号；underline 是其中一种具体的标记方式。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the two plain pieces of the compound and the situations where the word really appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个复合词的两个朴素部件，以及这个词真正出现的场合。

normal.en: under plus line: draw the line under the words.
normal.cn: under 加 line：把线画在字的下方。

normal.en: A teacher says underline it, and the class reaches for a ruler.
normal.cn: 老师说把这个词划出来，全班就去拿尺子。

normal.en: Highlight uses colour, underline uses a stroke.
normal.cn: highlight 用颜色，underline 用笔画。

normal.en: Underlined links are the old look of the web.
normal.cn: 带下划线的链接是网页早年常见的样子。

normal.en: A fact that underlines a problem makes it impossible to overlook.
normal.cn: underline 一个问题，就是让这个问题无法被忽略。

abstract.en: Think of a sheet of paper with one line pressed into it: everything above the line is what you must not miss.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸被压出一道线：线以上的内容就是你绝不能漏掉的部分。

abstract.en: The stroke can leave the paper: a silent empty hall underlines what nobody dared to say.
abstract.cn: 这道笔画可以离开纸面：空荡无声的大厅会强调谁也不敢说出口的话。

abstract.en: To underline is to choose: out of a whole page, one line is singled out to be seen.
abstract.cn: 划线就是选择：整页之中，只有一行被挑出来被看见。

examples.en: Please underline the words you do not know.
examples.cn: 请把你不认识的词划上横线。

examples.en: The mayor underlined that no new taxes would be raised this year.
examples.cn: 市长强调今年不会新增税收。

examples.en: Thin ice round the pond underlines the danger of skating there.
examples.cn: 池塘边薄薄的冰更凸显出在那里滑冰的危险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的莱恩」——安把莱恩的名字在纸下划了一道线：划下划线、强调

root: 由本土介词 under（古英语 under，在下面）与拉丁语 linea（麻线、线，经古法语 ligne 入英语）组成，字面即「在字下画线」，近代英语才合成此词。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of underline all keep one gesture: a stroke placed beneath something so that it stands apart from what surrounds it.
sensesIntro.cn: underline 的五个义项都保留同一个动作：在某物下方画一道笔画，让它从周围脱离出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen draws a straight stroke right beneath a word on the page.
core.cn: 核心意象：笔在纸上的一个词下方画出笔直的一道线。

branches.en: THE PAGE: the hand draws the line under a word.
branches.cn: 纸面线：手在词的下方画出这条线。

branches.en: THE MARK: the stroke becomes a visible sign, and printed text can carry it already.
branches.cn: 标记线：笔画成为可见的标记，印刷文字也可以自带这道线。

branches.en: THE VOICE: stressing a point does with speech what the line does with ink.
branches.cn: 声音线：强调某点是用言语做这道线用墨水做的事。

branches.en: THE BACKGROUND: what is underlined stands out from everything around it.
branches.cn: 背景线：被划线之物从周围一切中凸显出来。

branches.en: THE GESTURE: from a school exercise to a warning sign, the same downward stroke is repeated.
branches.cn: 动作线：从课堂练习到警示信号，重复的都是同一道向下压的笔画。

intro.en: The compound is transparent: an English preposition plus a Latin noun, with ordinary suffixes for the rest of the family.
intro.cn: 这个复合词结构透明：一个英语介词加一个拉丁语名词，词族其余成员用普通后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin linea is recorded and came to English through Old French ligne; only the deeper root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 linea 有文献记录，经古法语 ligne 进入英语；只有更早的词根属于重构。

items.example: The prefix places the stroke lower than the letters.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把笔画放在字母的下方。

items.example: The noun names the stroke that gets drawn.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被画出的那道笔画。

items.example: The Latin noun named the mason's cord.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词原指工匠用的麻绳。

items.example: French carried the noun into English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个名词带进英语。

items.example: A close synonym built the same way.
items.exampleCN: 用同样方式构成的近义词。

items.example: The opposite kind of line, around rather than below.
items.exampleCN: 方向相反的另一种线：绕在外面而不是压在下边。

items.example: The word is its own best example.
items.exampleCN: 这个词本身就是自己最好的例子。

latinEntries.structure: Old French noun from Latin linea

definition_zh: 乘船游览；巡航；以稳定速度行驶
definition_en: to travel by ship for pleasure, or to move at a steady, easy speed
core_image: 白色游轮贴着蓝色海面缓缓滑过
scene: 白色游轮贴着海面缓缓滑过，甲板上的人晒着太阳。 They cruise along the coast for a week each summer.
sceneCN: 这里 cruise 指「乘船游览」（第 1 个义项：为休闲而坐船航行）；句意是每年夏天他们沿着海岸巡游一周。

pos.zh: 乘船游览；巡航；以稳定速度行驶

derivatives.zh: 巡洋舰；游艇
巡航；乘船游览

senses.title: A pleasure voyage
senses.definition: a holiday trip by ship, or to make such a trip
senses.definitionCN: 坐船度假的旅行，或进行这样的旅行
senses.example: We took a cruise around the islands.
senses.exampleCN: 我们绕着群岛坐船玩了一圈。
senses.why: A ship turns travel itself into the destination.
senses.whyCN: 船让旅途本身变成目的地。

senses.title: Steady patrolling
senses.definition: to sail or fly on a fixed route for patrol or duty
senses.definitionCN: 沿固定路线航行或飞行以巡逻、执勤
senses.example: Two ships cruise the bay every night.
senses.exampleCN: 两艘船每晚在海湾巡航。
senses.why: A route walked again and again becomes a duty.
senses.whyCN: 同一条路线一遍遍走，就成了职责。

senses.title: A steady speed
senses.definition: to move or drive at a steady, easy speed
senses.definitionCN: 以平稳省力的速度移动或驾驶
senses.example: The car cruises at ninety on the open road.
senses.exampleCN: 这车在开阔路上以九十匀速行驶。
senses.why: At one easy speed, the machine stops fighting the road.
senses.whyCN: 保持一个省力的速度，机器就不再和路较劲。

intro.en: Cruise comes from Dutch kruisen, to cross, from Latin crux, a cross; a ship that crosses back and forth is cruising.
intro.cn: cruise 源自荷兰语 kruisen（横过、交叉），更早出自拉丁语 crux（十字）；船来回横过海面，就是巡航。

items.en: Kruisen meant to cross or move to and fro.
items.cn: kruisen 意为横过或来回移动。

items.en: It came from crux, a cross, the shape of crossing lines.
items.cn: 它出自 crux（十字），即交叉线的形状。

items.en: To cruise was to sail to and fro in search of ships.
items.cn: cruise 指在海上来回航行以搜寻船只。

items.en: Steam ships made cruising a pleasure trip.
items.cn: 汽船让巡航变成了休闲旅行。

items.en: Cars and planes now cruise at a steady speed.
items.cn: 如今汽车与飞机也以稳定速度巡航。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cru- opening and the -ise ending, and the meaning group names other journeys on water.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cru- 开头与 -ise 结尾，近义组列出其他水上旅程的说法。

entries.definition: a fast warship or a motor boat
entries.definitionCN: 快速军舰或摩托艇

entries.definition: a dark mark on the skin
entries.definitionCN: 皮肤上的青紫伤

entries.definition: a small bottle for oil or vinegar
entries.definitionCN: 装油或醋的小瓶

entries.definition: a long journey by sea
entries.definitionCN: 海上长途航行

entries.definition: to travel on water by wind
entries.definitionCN: 借风在水上航行

entries.definition: to move around an area to guard it
entries.definitionCN: 在某区域巡视守卫

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a white ship on flat water and end with a car holding one easy speed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一艘在平静海面上的白船开始，落到一辆保持匀速的车。

normal.en: A cruise is a journey that has become the destination.
normal.cn: 乘船巡游，是旅途本身变成了目的地。

normal.en: The ship crosses the sea and calls it a holiday.
normal.cn: 船横过海面，把这叫作假期。

normal.en: Cruise control lets the car keep one steady speed.
normal.cn: 定速巡航让车保持一个稳定的速度。

normal.en: To cruise is to cross without hurry.
normal.cn: cruise 就是不慌不忙地横过去。

normal.en: A cruiser is either a warship or a fast boat.
normal.cn: cruiser 不是军舰就是快艇。

abstract.en: Picture a white ship cutting a long line in blue water.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘白船在蓝色海面上划出长线。

abstract.en: Picture a deck chair and a book left open.
abstract.cn: 想象一张甲板椅和一本摊开的书。

abstract.en: Picture a needle holding one speed on the dial.
abstract.cn: 想象指针在表盘上定住一个速度。

examples.en: They cruise the islands every winter.
examples.cn: 他们每年冬天乘船游群岛。

examples.en: The ship cruised slowly past the harbour.
examples.cn: 船缓缓驶过港口。

examples.en: He put the car in cruise and relaxed.
examples.cn: 他打开定速巡航，放松下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cruise 记成「横过去」：cru 是十字（crux），船横过海面，就成了巡游。

root: 源自荷兰语 kruisen（横过、交叉），更早出自拉丁语 crux（十字）；本义是在海面上来回横越，后指巡航，再引申为乘车船从容行进。

sensesIntro.en: From crossing the sea to patrolling it, then to any steady motion.
sensesIntro.cn: 从横越海面，到在海面巡逻，再到任何平稳的行进。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white ship drawing a slow line across blue water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一艘白船在蓝色海面上划出缓慢的线。

branches.en: A crossing made for pleasure becomes a holiday.
branches.cn: 为享乐而做的横越，成了假期。

branches.en: A route sailed again and again becomes a patrol.
branches.cn: 一遍遍走的航线，成了巡逻。

branches.en: One easy speed is a cruise on any road.
branches.cn: 一个省力的速度，在任何路上都叫巡航。

branches.en: Pleasure trips and patrols both keep crossing the water.
branches.cn: 游船与巡逻都在不断横过水面。

branches.en: Steady motion is the thread under all three senses.
branches.cn: 平稳的行进是这三个义项共同的线。

intro.en: Cruise and cruiser belong to the Latin crux, a cross, the shape of a route that crosses water.
intro.cn: cruise 与 cruiser 属于拉丁语 crux（十字）一族，那是航线横过水面的形状。

latinIntro.en: The Latin crux, a cross, is the root under cruise and cross alike.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 crux（十字）是 cruise 与 cross 共同的根。

items.example: They cruise the coast in summer.

items.meaning: a fast warship or motor boat

a large ship for holiday trips

to go from one side to the other

items.meaningCN: 为某种主张的长久斗争
items.example: She led a crusade for clean water.
items.exampleCN: 她发起了一场争取干净水的运动。

items.example: The story says they crucified him.
items.exampleCN: 故事说他们把他钉上了十字架。

definition_en: to develop factories and large-scale production in a country or area
core_image: 田野旁立起新的厂房，烟囱冒出第一缕烟
scene: 一个农业小镇，几年间盖起了工厂。 The government wanted to industrialize the poor region within a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 industrialize 是「使工业化」（第 1 个义项：使某地发展起工业）；句意是政府想用十年时间让这个贫困地区实现工业化。

pos.zh: 动词：使工业化；使产业化

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -ation，义为「工业化」
去掉动词词尾，义为「工业的」
加表人后缀 -ist，义为「工业家」
词根名词，义为「工业；行业」

senses.title: To bring industry to a place
senses.definition: to build factories and manufacturing in a place that had little of them
senses.definitionCN: 在原本缺少工业的地方建立工厂与制造业
senses.example: The plan was to industrialize the southern provinces.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划是要让南方各省工业化。
senses.why: The verb is simply industry made into an action: causing industry to exist.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是把 industry 变成动作：促使工业存在。

senses.title: To change production by machines
senses.definition: to replace handwork with machines and factory organization
senses.definitionCN: 用手工改为机器与工厂组织
senses.example: Farming in the valley was industrialized after the railway came.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路到来之后，山谷里的农业实现了工厂化。
senses.why: Not only countries but whole kinds of work can be pushed into factories.
senses.whyCN: 不只是国家，整类劳动也能被推进工厂体制。

senses.title: To become industrial
senses.definition: to develop into an industrial economy, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 不带宾语时，表示自身发展成为工业经济
senses.example: The country industrialized faster than its neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家比邻国更快实现了工业化。
senses.why: When the change happens by itself, the verb drops its object.
senses.whyCN: 当变化自行发生时，动词就省掉了宾语。

senses.title: To be organized like a factory
senses.titleCN: 被像工厂那样组织起来
senses.definition: to make an activity standardized, large and machine-run
senses.definitionCN: 使某项活动标准化、大规模化、机器化
senses.example: Some critics say the school has been industrialized.
senses.exampleCN: 一些批评者说这所学校已经被工厂化了。
senses.why: The metaphor extends beyond economics into any activity made mechanical.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻超出经济领域，延伸到任何被机械化的活动。

intro.en: Industrialize is a modern verb built from industrial, itself from Latin industria, with the productive suffix -ize.
intro.cn: industrialize 是近代动词，由 industrial 加能产后缀 -ize 构成，而 industrial 又出自拉丁语 industria。

items.en: Industria meant diligence, built on indu, or in, plus struere, to build.
items.cn: industria 意为勤勉，由 indu（或 in）加 struere（建造）构成。

items.en: The word reached English as industrie, meaning skill or a trade.
items.cn: 这个词以 industrie 的形式进入英语，意为技艺或行业。

items.en: Industry came to name large-scale manufacturing in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 十八世纪 industry 开始指大规模制造。

items.en: -ize, from Greek through Latin, was added to industrial to make the action.
items.cn: -ize 经拉丁语源自希腊语，被加到 industrial 上构成动作。

items.en: Industrialize spread in the nineteenth century as nations pushed to build factories.
items.cn: 十九世纪各国争相建厂，industrialize 随之流行。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the industrial family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of economic change.
note.cn: 形近组收 industrial 一词族；近义组收描述经济变化的动词。

entries.definition: The process of building industry.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「工业化」，是 industrialize 的名词形式。

entries.definition: Relating to factories and production.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「工业的」，是动词的来源。

entries.definition: Working hard and steadily.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「勤劳的」，只是同根而含义不同。

entries.definition: To bring up to date with new methods.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使现代化」，与工业化常同时发生。

entries.definition: To replace human work with machines.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使机械化」，强调机器替代人手。

entries.definition: To grow or make something grow bigger.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发展」，是更宽泛的说法。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the -ize ending, the family of nouns and adjectives, and the picture of a country changing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借 -ize 词尾、同族名词形容词以及一个地区转变的画面。

normal.en: Take industrial, add -ize, and the adjective turns into a verb of change.
normal.cn: industrial 加 -ize，形容词就变成表示变化的动词。

normal.en: The noun form swaps -ize for -ization, so the process is industrialization.
normal.cn: 名词形式把 -ize 换成 -ization，过程就是 industrialization。

normal.en: Newly industrialized is common: it names countries that changed in recent decades.
normal.cn: newly industrialized 很常见，指近几十年才转变的国家。

normal.en: The verb can drop its object: a country can simply industrialize.
normal.cn: 这个动词可以省略宾语：一个国家可以自行工业化。

normal.en: The industria root still means diligence, so the word is hard work raised to a national scale.
normal.cn: industria 词根仍是勤勉，所以这个词是放大到国家尺度的努力。

abstract.en: Industrialize is a before and after word: fields on one side, chimneys on the other.
abstract.cn: industrialize 是一个前后对比的词：一边是田野，一边是烟囱。

abstract.en: To industrialize a thing is to make it run like a factory, even a school or a farm.
abstract.cn: 把某样东西工业化，就是让它像工厂一样运转，哪怕是一所学校或一片农场。

abstract.en: Every -ize verb carries an engine: it makes something happen to what follows.
abstract.cn: 每个 -ize 动词都带着一台发动机：它让后面的对象发生改变。

examples.en: The country began to industrialize after the war.
examples.cn: 这个国家在战后开始工业化。

examples.en: They hoped to industrialize the region without destroying its forests.
examples.cn: 他们希望在不破坏森林的前提下使该地区工业化。

examples.en: Cheap coal helped the area industrialize quickly.
examples.cn: 廉价的煤帮助这一地区迅速实现工业化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬打湿来子」——机器硬干活打湿了衣衫的来子，工厂就这样建起来。

root: industrial（工业的）+ -ize（使……化）；industrial 出自拉丁语 industria（勤勉）。

sensesIntro.en: Industrialize starts as bringing factories to a place and widens to mechanizing any work, to the self-driven change of a country and even to the factory-like ordering of daily life.
sensesIntro.cn: industrialize 起初指把工厂带到一个地方，随后扩展到使任何劳动机械化、一个国家自行转变，乃至把日常生活按工厂方式组织起来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first chimney rising beside a rice field.
core.cn: 核心意象：稻田旁升起第一根烟囱。

branches.en: PLACE LINE: factories are brought into a region.
branches.cn: 地点线：工厂被带进一片区域。

branches.en: MACHINE LINE: handwork gives way to machines.
branches.cn: 机器线：手工让位于机器。

branches.en: ECONOMY LINE: the change happens on its own, without an object.
branches.cn: 经济线：变化自行发生，不带宾语。

branches.en: SYSTEM LINE: anything can be run like a factory.
branches.cn: 系统线：任何事物都能像工厂那样运作。

branches.en: PRODUCTION LINE: factories and machines together remake output.
branches.cn: 生产线：工厂与机器合起来重塑产出。

intro.en: A verb made with the productive -ize suffix on top of the industrial family.
intro.cn: 一个在 industrial 词族之上用能产后缀 -ize 构成的动词。

latinIntro.en: -ize comes from Greek -izein through Latin -izare, found in countless English verbs of change.
latinIntro.cn: -ize 经拉丁语 -izare 源自希腊语 -izein，出现在大量表示变化的英语动词中。

definition_en: coming after the sixty-ninth, or one of seventy equal parts
core_image: 纪念册翻到第七十页，页角是金色的数字
scene: 俱乐部庆祝了它的第七十周年。 The club celebrated its seventieth year.
sceneCN: 这里 seventieth 是「第七十」（第 1 个义项）；句意：俱乐部庆祝了它的第七十周年。

derivatives.zh: 七十
第七
七

senses.title: The seventieth in order
senses.definition: coming after the sixty-ninth in a series
senses.definitionCN: 在一系列中排在第六十九之后的
senses.example: The club celebrated its seventieth year.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部庆祝了它的第七十周年。
senses.why: This is the ordinal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是序数义项。

senses.title: One of seventy parts
senses.definition: one of seventy equal parts of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物被均分为七十份中的一份
senses.example: A seventieth of the total was set aside.
senses.exampleCN: 总数的七十分之一被留了出来。
senses.why: Ordinals also name fractions.
senses.whyCN: 序数词也能表示分数。

intro.en: Seventieth is seventy plus the ordinal suffix -th.
intro.cn: seventieth 是 seventy 加序数后缀 -th 构成。

items.en: Seofontig meant seventy.
items.cn: seofontig 意为七十。

items.en: Seventi took a clearer form.
items.cn: seventi 形成更清晰的形式。

items.en: Seventy settled its modern spelling.
items.cn: seventy 固定了现代拼写。

items.en: Seventieth named the ordinal.
items.cn: seventieth 成为序数词。

items.en: Seventieth also named a fraction.
items.cn: seventieth 也用来表示分数。

note.en: Seventieth is compared with similar-looking words and with other ordinals.
note.cn: 把 seventieth 与形近词以及其他序数词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Seventieth is the seventieth position or the seventieth share.
normalIntro.cn: seventieth 既是第七十个位置，也是第七十份份额。

normal.en: They celebrated a seventieth birthday.
normal.cn: 他们庆祝了七十岁生日。

normal.en: The seventieth anniversary drew a crowd.
normal.cn: 七十周年纪念吸引了许多人。

normal.en: He finished seventieth in the marathon.
normal.cn: 他在马拉松中获得第七十名。

abstract.en: Seventy years is a lifetime measured in patience.
abstract.cn: 七十年，是用耐心丈量的一生。

abstract.en: An anniversary turns time into a shared object.
abstract.cn: 纪念日把时间变成了可以共享的物件。

abstract.en: Even the smallest share keeps a whole connected.
abstract.cn: 再小的份额，也维系着整体。

examples.en: The club celebrated its seventieth year.
examples.cn: 俱乐部庆祝了它的第七十周年。

examples.en: A seventieth of the total was set aside.
examples.cn: 总数的七十分之一被留了出来。

examples.en: They celebrated a seventieth birthday.
examples.cn: 他们庆祝了七十岁生日。

dict_mnemonic.text: seventieth 由 seventy（七十）加序数后缀 -th 构成，表示「第七十」或「七十分之一」。

root: 由古英语 seofontig（七十）加序数后缀演变而来。

sensesIntro.en: Seventieth means coming after the sixty-ninth or one of seventy equal parts.
sensesIntro.cn: seventieth 意为第七十或七十分之一。

core.en: The position or share that belongs to seventy.
core.cn: 与七十相关的位置或份额。

branches.en: The seventieth position.
branches.cn: 第七十个位置。

branches.en: One part out of seventy.
branches.cn: 七十份中的一份。

branches.en: Order and fraction share the suffix.
branches.cn: 顺序与分数共用同一个后缀。

branches.en: A milestone year.
branches.cn: 一个里程碑式的年份。

branches.en: A small share of a whole.
branches.cn: 整体中很小的一份。

intro.en: Seventieth is formed with the ordinal suffix -th on seventy.
intro.cn: seventieth 由 seventy 加序数后缀 -th 构成。

latinIntro.en: Seventieth has no Latin ancestor; Latin septuagesimus is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: seventieth 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 septuagesimus（第七十）只是语义对应词。

items.example: The land was divided into seventieths.
The song was popular in the seventies.
items.exampleCN: 这首歌在七十年代很流行。

definition_en: an assistant to a senior person, especially a political leader or military officer
core_image: 走在要人半步之后、随时递上文件的那个人
scene: 走廊尽头，一位年轻人快步跟上部长，把一张纸条递过去。 A senior aide handed the minister a note.
sceneCN: 这里 aide 是「（要人的）助手」（第 1 个义项：为高级人物处理事务的助理）；句意为一名高级助理把一张便条递给部长。图中可辨识物件：走廊、纸条、公文包。

pos.zh: 名词：（要人的）助手；助理；副官

derivatives.zh: 由法语借入的军事用语，义为「副官；侍从武官」
由法语借入的外交用语，义为「备忘录；备忘便览」

senses.title: An assistant to a senior figure
senses.definition: a person employed to assist a senior political figure or official, often handling information and arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 受雇协助高级政治人物或官员的人，常负责信息与事务安排
senses.example: A senior aide handed the minister a note.
senses.exampleCN: 一名高级助理把一张便条递给部长。
senses.why: The e was added in the nineteenth century to separate the person from aid 'help', so the spelling itself marks the human role.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪加上 e，是为了把「人」与表示「帮助」的 aid 区分开，所以拼写本身就标出了这个人的身份。

senses.title: A military officer attending a superior
senses.definition: an officer whose duty is to attend a senior officer and carry orders, in the phrase aide-de-camp
senses.definitionCN: 负责随侍上级军官并传达命令的军官，用于 aide-de-camp 一词
senses.example: The general's aide-de-camp rode ahead to warn the camp.
senses.exampleCN: 将军的副官骑马先行，去给营地报信。
senses.why: This is the older military sense, borrowed whole from French, and it keeps the full French phrase rather than the short English form.
senses.whyCN: 这是更早的军事义，整组从法语借来，因此保留完整法语短语，而不是缩成英语的短形式。

intro.en: Aide and aid are the same French word twice borrowed: once for help, once for the person who gives it.
intro.cn: aide 与 aid 是同一个法语词被借了两次：一次指帮助，一次指提供帮助的人。

items.en: Adiutare, 'to keep helping', is the Latin verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: adiutare「不断帮助」是这整个词族背后的拉丁动词。

items.en: Old French aide could mean 'help' or 'a helper', so one form served both ideas.
items.cn: 古法语 aide 既可指「帮助」，也可指「帮手」，一个形式承担两个意思。

items.en: English took the word as aid in the fourteenth century, using it for both the help and the helper.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪以 aid 的形式借入，既指帮助也指帮手。

items.en: The spelling aide was revived for the personal assistant, following the French spelling, to keep the two roles apart.
items.cn: 十九世纪依照法语拼写重新启用 aide 专指私人助理，以便把两种角色分开。

items.en: Aide now covers political staff and, in the full French phrase, military officers, while aid stays with help in general.
items.cn: 如今 aide 指政治幕僚，在完整法语短语中亦指军官，而 aid 仍指一般意义上的帮助。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words confused with aide in spelling; the near-meaning group gathers people who assist, with different ranks.
note.cn: 形近组收易与 aide 拼写混淆的词；近义组收提供协助的人，身份层级各不相同。

entries.definition: Help itself, or the act of helping.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助本身，或提供帮助的行为。

entries.definition: A military officer who attends a senior officer.
entries.definitionCN: 随侍高级军官的军官。

entries.definition: A memorandum, or a document used to help the memory.
entries.definitionCN: 备忘录，或帮助记忆的文件。

entries.definition: A person who helps someone in their work, at any level.
entries.definitionCN: 在工作中帮助他人的人，层级不限。

entries.definition: A person whose role is to give expert advice.
entries.definitionCN: 专门提供专业建议的人。

entries.definition: A person who acts for a superior when needed.
entries.definitionCN: 在需要时代理上级职务的人。

normalIntro.en: Two real parts carry the word: the French noun aide and the added e that marks a person.
normalIntro.cn: 两个真实部件承载这个词：法语名词 aide，以及用来标记「人」的那个 e。

normal.en: The e is the person: aide has someone in it, aid is just help.
normal.cn: 那个 e 就是人：aide 里装着一个人，aid 只是帮助。

normal.en: An aide walks half a step behind and carries the papers.
normal.cn: 助手总是落后半步，手里抱着文件。

normal.en: Aide-de-camp keeps the whole French phrase, so it looks long even though the short form is tiny.
normal.cn: aide-de-camp 保留整个法语短语，所以短形式虽短，它却很长。

normal.en: Say it exactly like aid: the e is silent.
normal.cn: 发音与 aid 完全相同：结尾的 e 不发音。

normal.en: Presidential aide, senior aide, close aide: the adjective tells you how near the power the person stands.
normal.cn: 总统助手、高级助理、亲信助手：前面的形容词说明这个人离权力有多近。

abstract.en: An aide turns help into a job: the same old idea of assistance, now with hours and duties.
abstract.cn: 助手把帮助变成了一份职业：同样是「协助」这个古老观念，现在有了工时和职责。

abstract.en: That the helper needed a separate spelling shows how much a society cares about distinguishing a person from an act.
abstract.cn: 连「帮手」都需要单独的拼写，说明社会有多在意把一个人与一个动作区分开。

abstract.en: Proximity is the aide's real power: standing close to the decision is often more useful than making it.
abstract.cn: 接近性正是助手的真正权力：站在决定旁边，往往比做决定更有用。

examples.en: A senior aide handed the minister a note.
examples.cn: 一名高级助理把一张便条递给部长。

examples.en: She worked as an aide to the mayor for three years.
examples.cn: 她给市长当了三年助手。

examples.en: The general's aide-de-camp rode ahead to warn the camp.
examples.cn: 将军的副官骑马先行，去给营地报信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶的」——诶，得有个助理在旁边递文件。

root: 源自古法语 aide「帮助、帮手」，与 aid 同源；十九世纪依法语拼写重新启用 aide，专指要人的助理。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses name a person whose job is help: one in a political office, one on a general's staff.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都指以「帮助」为职责的人：一个在政治办公室里，一个在将军的幕僚中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young assistant half a step behind the senior figure, papers already in hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：年轻助手落后要人半步，文件已经拿在手里。

branches.en: a note passed in a corridor
branches.cn: 在走廊里递过去的一张便条

branches.en: a campaign worker keeping a candidate on time
branches.cn: 让候选人准时的竞选工作人员

branches.en: an officer riding ahead with orders
branches.cn: 带着命令先行出发的军官

branches.en: a uniform waiting at the door of a staff car
branches.cn: 在指挥车门口等候的军装

branches.en: one attending role, in civil and in military dress
branches.cn: 同一个随侍角色，一身文职、一身军装

intro.en: The French noun aide, its Latin verb, and the compound phrases French handed to English whole.
intro.cn: 法语名词 aide、其拉丁动词，以及法语整组交给英语的复合短语。

latinIntro.en: adiutare is recorded Latin; the French forms are medieval, and the military phrase is later still.
latinIntro.cn: adiutare 是有文献记录的拉丁词；法语形式属中世纪，军事短语出现更晚。
